answers.C: Increase number of epochs to convergence
answers.D: Train on spot instances only

explanation: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (adapters, LoRA) reduces compute cycles substantially, cutting energy use. Larger GPUs helps but still full-model training; more epochs increase carbon; spot instances affect cost, not total energy.

stem: Your fine-tuning job on Amazon SageMaker fails due to out-of-memory errors on 8-GPU instances. Which solution reduces memory footprint without degrading performance?

answers.A: Enable gradient checkpointing
answers.B: Reduce batch size to 1
answers.C: Disable mixed-precision training
answers.D: Increase model parallelism chunks to more GPUs

explanation: Gradient checkpointing trades compute for memory, allowing larger models to train without OOM. Batch size 1 slows convergence; disabling mixed precision increases memory; more GPUs adds cost and complexity but checkpointing is first fix.

stem: You must fine-tune a foundation model while ensuring fairness across demographic groups. Which data preparation tactic helps?

answers.A: Oversample majority group examples
answers.B: Use stratified sampling to balance demographic representation
answers.C: Mask demographic tokens during training
answers.D: Train separate models per demographic

explanation: Stratified sampling balances training data across demographics. Oversampling majority worsens imbalance; masking tokens removes context; separate models increase maintenance and complicate fairness across groups.

stem: A developer fine-tunes a code generation foundation model and wants to measure the percentage of generated functions that compile and pass unit tests. Which evaluation metric best captures this requirement?

answers.A: BLEU
answers.B: pass@k
answers.C: Cyclomatic complexity
answers.D: Perplexity

explanation: pass@k directly measures the fraction of samples that pass testing under k attempts, reflecting functional correctness rather than surface similarity or code complexity.

stem: You need to benchmark two multilingual translation foundation models across multiple language pairs. Which dataset and metric combination is most appropriate?

answers.A: WMT and BLEU
answers.B: GLUE and ROUGE
answers.C: SQuAD and BERTScore
answers.D: COCO and METEOR

explanation: The WMT (Workshop on Machine Translation) dataset with BLEU is the industry standard for evaluating machine translation quality across language pairs.

stem: When evaluating paraphrased customer support responses, which metric accounts for synonym usage and paraphrase quality over exact word overlap?

answers.A: BLEU
answers.B: ROUGE
answers.C: Exact match
answers.D: METEOR

explanation: METEOR incorporates stemming and synonym matching, making it better for paraphrase evaluation than surface-overlap metrics like BLEU or ROUGE.

stem: For a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application, which pair of evaluation metrics best measure retrieval accuracy and subsequent generation quality?

answers.A: BLEU and perplexity
answers.B: Recall@k and ROUGE
answers.C: Accuracy and F1
answers.D: Precision and recall

explanation: Recall@k evaluates how often relevant documents are retrieved, and ROUGE assesses the quality of the generated text given those documents.

stem: To monitor drift in a deployed foundation model’s outputs over time, which evaluation approach is most appropriate?

answers.A: Cross-validation with multiple folds
answers.B: Periodic human review of sampled outputs
answers.C: Single-run perplexity measurement
answers.D: Monitoring parameter count

explanation: Periodic human review identifies qualitative shifts or biases in outputs that automated metrics might miss, making it essential for drift detection.

stem: For evaluating translation at the character level to better handle morphologically rich languages, which metric should you use?

answers.A: BLEU
answers.B: ROUGE
answers.C: FID
answers.D: chrF

explanation: chrF calculates F-scores over character n-grams, improving evaluation for languages with complex morphology compared to word-based metrics.

stem: To evaluate factual consistency automatically, which specialized tool or metric should you use?

answers.A: Perplexity
answers.B: BLEU
answers.C: ROUGE
answers.D: FactCC

explanation: FactCC uses a classifier to detect factual errors in generated text, providing an automated measure of factual consistency.

stem: To evaluate a multilingual retrieval-augmented generation system, which combined metrics should be used for retrieval effectiveness and generated text quality?

answers.A: MRR and BERTScore
answers.B: BLEU and Perplexity
answers.C: FID and ROUGE
answers.D: Accuracy and F1

explanation: MRR measures retrieval ranking quality, and BERTScore evaluates semantic quality of the generated text in multiple languages.

stem: A financial services company uses a SageMaker Clarify pre-training bias analysis and finds a high Statistical Parity Difference (SPD) for a protected group. Which next step best mitigates bias at the dataset level?

answers.A: Apply class weighting during model training to penalize misclassifications for the protected group.
answers.B: Inject synthetic samples of the protected group after model training to balance outputs.
answers.C: Use stratified sampling or data augmentation to increase representation of the under-represented group before retraining.
answers.D: Adjust the decision threshold post-inference to equalize positive rates across groups.

explanation: Mitigating SPD bias at the dataset level requires increasing representation via stratified sampling or augmentation prior to training. Other options address bias post-training or at inference.

stem: An e-commerce retailer is concerned about model overfitting and lack of robustness when training a computer vision model. Which combination of responsible AI practices most directly addresses variance risk?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to detect drift and apply differential privacy during training.
answers.B: Implement RLHF and use Bedrock Guardrails to enforce safety constraints.
answers.C: Apply data pruning and use a larger transformer foundation model for high accuracy.
answers.D: Augment training images for diversity and use k-fold cross-validation to measure generalization.

explanation: Augmenting data increases diversity reducing variance, while k-fold cross-validation assesses generalization. Other options address drift, privacy, or performance but not variance.

stem: A legal team warns that a fine-tuned foundation model may produce outputs infringing third-party IP. Which responsible AI control best reduces IP infringement risk?

answers.A: Implement content filtering using Bedrock Guardrails to block copyrighted text generation.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Clarify to identify copyright in the training data.
answers.C: Apply differential privacy during fine-tuning to obscure original data.
answers.D: Deploy Model Monitor to detect IP patterns in inference logs.

explanation: Bedrock Guardrails enforce rules at generation time to block copyrighted outputs. Clarify and privacy techniques address bias/data privacy, not IP output control.

stem: A model deployed on SageMaker shows a rising False Positive Rate (FPR) for a minority group over time. Which AWS capability and metric should the team use to detect this fairness drift?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify post-training: monitor AUC separately for each group.
answers.B: SageMaker Model Monitor: configure a bias drift job to track group-specific FPR over time.
answers.C: Amazon A2I: route predictions for the minority group to human reviewers.
answers.D: SageMaker Debugger: set up rule to detect increased loss for the minority group.

explanation: Model Monitor’s bias drift jobs can track fairness metrics like group-specific FPR. Clarify is offline, A2I routes for human review but does not detect drift automatically, Debugger tracks training metrics.

stem: An organization must document data lineage and responsible AI decisions across the ML pipeline. Which AWS service combination provides end-to-end lineage and audit capabilities?

answers.A: AWS Config to track resource changes and SageMaker Clarify for bias reports.
answers.B: AWS CloudTrail for API activity and Amazon Macie for data classification.
answers.C: SageMaker Model Monitor for drift and Amazon Inspector for vulnerabilities.
answers.D: AWS Glue Data Catalog for metadata lineage and AWS CloudTrail for audit logs.

explanation: Glue Data Catalog captures dataset metadata and lineage; CloudTrail logs API calls and workflow steps for audits. Other options address security or bias reporting but not full lineage.

stem: A healthcare provider needs to ensure its model does not discriminate by gender. They require transparency of feature impact. Which approach best delivers explainability and bias detection?

answers.A: Use Amazon A2I to have clinicians label misclassifications by gender.
answers.B: Train with differential privacy to avoid encoding gender information.
answers.C: Use SageMaker Clarify’s SHAP explainability to measure gender’s feature importance and bias metrics.
answers.D: Configure Bedrock Guardrails to block gender-related outputs.

explanation: Clarify SHAP provides feature impact and bias metrics for sensitive attributes. A2I handles human review, privacy training obfuscates but not explains, Guardrails block outputs, not explain model internals.

stem: A startup chooses between a large foundation model and a smaller custom model. To minimize environmental impact while meeting 95% of their accuracy target, which responsible AI strategy should they apply?

answers.A: Use the large foundation model with reduced precision (FP16) and no fine-tuning.
answers.B: Benchmark both models for energy consumption per inference and select the smaller custom model if its accuracy meets the target.
answers.C: Host the large model on GPU-powered instances with auto-scaling to reduce idle time.
answers.D: Apply on-device inference to the foundation model to eliminate data center emissions.

explanation: Benchmarking energy per inference and choosing the smallest model that meets accuracy minimizes environmental impact. Precision and hosting strategies affect cost/performance but don't directly measure impact.

stem: A government agency needs to ensure ML model decisions are explainable to comply with regulations. Which AWS tool and practice combination supports this requirement?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to generate Model Cards and SHAP explainability reports.
answers.B: Leverage Amazon A2I to have domain experts annotate each decision.
answers.C: Deploy foundation models via Bedrock with no customization for transparency.
answers.D: Store all inference logs in Amazon S3 for manual auditing later.

explanation: Clarify Model Cards and SHAP reports provide structured model documentation and feature-level explainability. A2I reviews specific instances but not full model transparency; logs alone aren’t sufficient.

stem: A fraud detection model exhibits high variance yet low bias. Which dataset characteristic adjustment most directly reduces variance?

answers.A: Ensure the dataset is demographically representative by adding minority samples.
answers.B: Increase overall dataset size by collecting more varied fraudulent/non-fraudulent examples.
answers.C: Remove features highly correlated with the target variable to simplify the model.
answers.D: Adjust the decision threshold to favor reducing false positives.

explanation: High variance is reduced by increasing dataset size and diversity. Adding minority samples addresses bias. Feature removal and threshold adjustments address complexity and operating point, not variance.

stem: During bias detection, a team discovers a proxy variable highly correlated with sensitive attribute. Which responsible AI action best addresses this issue?

answers.A: Mask the sensitive attribute at inference to prevent discrimination.
answers.B: Use RLHF to teach the model fairness constraints.
answers.C: Remove or de-correlate the proxy variable from the training dataset.
answers.D: Adjust class weights during training to counter the proxy effect.

explanation: Removing or de-correlating the proxy variable prevents the model from learning unintended sensitive correlations. Masking at inference doesn’t retrain, RLHF isn’t designed for bias removal, class weights address imbalance but not proxy variables.

stem: A voice assistant model trained on English data shows poor performance and bias when used in a non-English region. Which dataset curation practice most responsibly addresses this outcome?

answers.A: Deploy an English foundation model with higher capacity GPUs to improve recognition.
answers.B: Use Bedrock Guardrails to translate non-English inputs to English before inference.
answers.C: Apply post-processing to normalize accents in the English transcripts.
answers.D: Collect and include diverse voice data from the target region to retrain or fine-tune the model.

explanation: Collecting and including regional voice data ensures diversity and reduces bias. Other options patch translation or normalization without addressing dataset deficiency.

stem: An NLP model fine-tuned on user reviews shows unexpected bias towards negative sentiment for a demographic. Which Clarify metric pair best identifies both bias and explainability issues?

answers.A: Post-training bias analysis with Disparate Impact and SHAP feature importance for demographic tokens.
answers.B: Pre-training bias analysis with Chi-squared test and LIME for local explanations.
answers.C: Model monitor with data quality checks and concept drift detection.
answers.D: A2I simulation to route negative sentiment for human audit and RLHF to adjust behavior.

explanation: Post-training bias analysis with Disparate Impact quantifies bias; SHAP explains feature contributions. Pre-training analysis doesn’t reflect model; other options don’t cover both bias and explainability.

stem: A social media platform wants to ensure its content recommendation model is robust and fair. Which multi-step approach correctly applies responsible AI practices?

answers.A: Deploy bedrock foundation model with no customization, then monitor user complaints.
answers.B: Use diverse training data, perform Clarify bias analysis, then implement Model Monitor for drift and fairness metrics.
answers.C: Apply RLHF to incorporate user feedback, then use A2I to human-review flagged recommendations.
answers.D: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect hate speech and apply Bedrock Guardrails to block content.

explanation: Diverse data plus Clarify bias analysis and Model Monitor drift checks covers training data fairness, bias validation, and ongoing monitoring. Other options focus only on feedback loops or content filtering.

stem: An energy company must choose between batch and real-time inference to reduce carbon footprint. Which responsible AI consideration should guide their choice?

answers.A: Real-time inference ensures fairness by updating model with live data.
answers.B: Batch inference simplifies explainability by aggregating predictions.
answers.C: Batch inference on low-usage off-peak times reduces energy consumption compared to always-on real-time endpoints.
answers.D: Real-time inference allows Guardrails to block hallucinations instantly.

explanation: Batch inference during off-peak reduces energy use, aligning with sustainability goals. Real-time addresses performance and safety but uses constant compute.

stem: A hiring platform’s resume screening model shows high false negative rates for a protected group. Which fairness metric adjustment and mitigation step is appropriate?

answers.A: Optimize for equalized odds by balancing FPR across groups via post-processing calibration.
answers.B: Target equal opportunity by adjusting threshold to equalize True Positive Rate (TPR) for the protected group.
answers.C: Use DP-SGD during training to ensure differential privacy for all candidates.
answers.D: Deploy Clarify’s pre-training bias report and retrain on a larger dataset.

explanation: Equal opportunity focuses on equal TPR; adjusting thresholds post-training targets false negatives. Equalized odds balances both FPR and FNR; DP-SGD addresses privacy, not fairness; pre-training bias doesn’t guarantee TPR parity.

stem: A model serving medical diagnoses must be auditable for bias and quality. Which combination of AWS services automates bias detection and logging at inference time?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify with server-side inference wrappers and CloudWatch Logs for real-time bias metrics.
answers.B: Amazon A2I for human-in-the-loop and S3 event notifications for logs.
answers.C: Model Monitor batch jobs scheduled hourly and AWS Config for configuration logs.
answers.D: Bedrock Guardrails for diagnosis validation and CloudTrail for API logs.

explanation: Combining Clarify in inference wrappers emits bias metrics, and CloudWatch Logs captures them. Model Monitor process is offline. A2I is human review, not automatic detection. Guardrails validate content but not bias metrics.

stem: A company trains a sentiment analysis model on customer feedback. They discover the model overfits on lengthier negative reviews. Which responsible AI technique addresses this bias?

answers.A: Use A2I to filter out long negative reviews during inference.
answers.B: Implement Bedrock Guardrails to normalize output sentiment scores.
answers.C: Apply length-based sampling or reweighting in the training set to balance review lengths.
answers.D: Fine-tune the model further with more negative samples.

explanation: Balancing training samples by review length addresses overfitting to long texts. A2I and Guardrails act at inference; more negative samples reinforce, not fix length bias.

stem: An AI image classification pipeline uses Amazon A2I. Which workflow change enhances responsible AI by reducing human bias in reviews?

answers.A: Provide diverse annotator pools and rotate assignments to minimize individual bias.
answers.B: Only route low-confidence images for review without systematic sampling.
answers.C: Use fixed guidelines without updating them to ensure consistency.
answers.D: Increase the AI confidence threshold to reduce human interventions.

explanation: Diverse annotators and rotation reduce individual biases. Routing only low-confidence may miss systematic errors; fixed guidelines become outdated; raising threshold reduces oversight.

stem: A transportation firm must ensure their ML model aligns with environmental sustainability guidelines. Which metric and AWS feature should they monitor?

answers.A: Track energy consumption per batch inference via SageMaker Debugger and AWS CloudWatch metrics.
answers.B: Monitor carbon emission estimates from Bedrock Guardrails.
answers.C: Use Clarify to report environmental bias in the dataset.
answers.D: Implement A2I to sample inferences for manual sustainability audits.

explanation: SageMaker Debugger profiles training/inference resource usage; CloudWatch aggregates metrics, enabling monitoring of energy consumption. Guardrails and Clarify don’t provide sustainability metrics.

stem: An AI system must comply with an accountability law requiring proof of non-discrimination. Which deliverable best demonstrates compliance?

answers.A: Stored inference logs in S3 with anonymized user IDs.
answers.B: A2I human review transcripts for flagged inferences.
answers.C: Generated Model Card from SageMaker Clarify including bias metrics and mitigation steps.
answers.D: Bedrock Guardrails configuration file showing blocked content rules.

explanation: A Model Card documents model details, bias metrics, and mitigation, serving as formal proof. Logs and reviews are raw data; Guardrails config shows rules but not measured bias.

stem: A retail AI solution applies oversampling of under-represented class, causing overfitting. Which strategy maintains dataset balance while reducing overfitting risk?

answers.A: Switch to SMOTE to generate synthetic minority samples without real data.
answers.B: Combine controlled undersampling of majority and slight oversampling of minority, followed by cross-validation.
answers.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to mask minority class labels during training.
answers.D: Increase model regularization hyperparameters until overfitting subsides.

explanation: Balanced undersampling and moderate oversampling reduces class imbalance and overfitting; SMOTE can introduce noise; masking labels corrupts data; regularization alone may not address imbalance.

stem: A company fine-tunes a foundation model on user data containing PII. Which responsible AI step ensures privacy compliance before fine-tuning?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to detect PII entities in training data and remove or anonymize them.
answers.B: Enable Bedrock Guardrails to block PII during inference.
answers.C: Configure Model Monitor to alert on PII patterns in logs.
answers.D: Rely on Data Catalog policies to quarantine sensitive buckets.

explanation: Clarify PII detection can identify and remove/anonymize PII pre-training. Guardrails and Model Monitor act post-deployment; Data Catalog policies manage storage, not data content.

stem: A model shows underfitting due to overly strict fairness constraints during training. Which mitigation balances fairness with performance?

answers.A: Remove all fairness constraints and retrain on raw data.
answers.B: Increase penalty weight on fairness loss to reduce bias further.
answers.C: Apply differential privacy to reduce model complexity.
answers.D: Relax fairness constraint hyperparameter slightly and monitor performance vs bias trade-off.

explanation: Relaxing constraint hyperparameter allows model to trade a bit more bias for performance. Removing constraints violates fairness; increasing penalty worsens underfitting; privacy doesn’t address fairness/performance trade-off.

stem: A content moderation model must detect emerging hate speech terms. Which AWS service and practice support ongoing dataset curation?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Clarify analyzers to detect new terms in training data.
answers.B: Implement Amazon Kendra on user reports to discover new terms, then retrain model periodically.
answers.C: Configure Bedrock Guardrails to ban any unknown terms automatically.
answers.D: Rely on Model Monitor drift detection to alert on lexical shifts.

explanation: Kendra can index user reports to surface new terms; human in the loop identifies them for dataset updates. Clarify doesn’t detect emergent terms; Guardrails ban known rules; drift detection alerts but requires manual term discovery.

stem: Which combination of AWS services and tasks demonstrates end-to-end responsible AI for a fraud detection pipeline?

answers.A: Glue Data Catalog for lineage, SageMaker Clarify for bias analysis, Model Monitor for drift, and CloudTrail for audit logs.
answers.B: Amazon A2I for human review, Bedrock for model serving, WAF for security, and Cost Explorer for cost analytics.
answers.C: AWS Config for configuration management, Amazon Comprehend for NLP, RDS for storage, and Inspector for vulnerability scanning.
answers.D: SageMaker JumpStart for model templates, S3 for data storage, CloudFront for delivery, and Macie for data classification.

explanation: Glue Data Catalog tracks data lineage; Clarify performs bias analysis; Model Monitor checks drift; CloudTrail logs activities, covering responsible AI. Other combinations miss key responsibilities.

stem: A model’s predictions must be fair across subgroups; the team chooses Demographic Parity. Which operational step ensures this fairness definition is maintained?

answers.A: Implement RLHF to shape model behavior according to parity.
answers.B: Add a bias-aware post-processing component to adjust prediction probabilities to match subgroup rates.
answers.C: Use differential privacy during training to equalize distributions.
answers.D: Apply Bedrock Guardrails to filter outputs by subgroup outcomes.

explanation: Post-processing adjustment aligns subgroup positive rates for Demographic Parity. RLHF, privacy, or Guardrails do not directly enforce statistical parity at output distribution.

stem: A loan approval model must demonstrate robustness against adversarial input perturbations. Which responsible AI technique helps achieve this?

answers.A: Use Clarify to detect adversarial examples in the training data.
answers.B: Deploy the model via Bedrock with Guardrails against malicious inputs.
answers.C: Include adversarial training samples in training set and retrain to increase robustness.
answers.D: Use Model Monitor to block anomalous inference requests.

explanation: Adversarial training augments training data with perturbed inputs to improve robustness. Clarify flags bias, not adversarial; Guardrails guard content, not adversarial attacks; Monitor blocks but doesn’t improve robustness.

stem: A fintech startup needs an AI model to score loan applications with high interpretability for regulators. They require per-feature contribution analysis. Which model and tool combination best balances transparency and predictive performance?

answers.A: Deep neural network with LIME
answers.B: Gradient Boosting Machine with SHAP values
answers.C: Logistic regression with no post-hoc analysis
answers.D: Transformer-based model with attention visualization

explanation: GBMs offer strong performance and SHAP provides consistent, global and local interpretability, unlike attention or none.

stem: A retail chain uses an LLM for product recommendations but regulators demand transparency. Which approach best improves explainability with minimal performance loss?

answers.A: Implement RAG with knowledge provenance and track token sources
answers.B: Fine-tune the LLM on proprietary data without documentation
answers.C: Switch entirely to a rule-based recommender
answers.D: Use closed-book LLM inference with opaque prompt templates

explanation: RAG captures source documents, improving transparency while preserving model strengths.

stem: A customer complaints model shows unexpected bias against a minority group. Which tool combination helps detect and mitigate this bias while maintaining explainability?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify for bias detection and Fairness Metrics
answers.B: SageMaker Autopilot for retraining without transparency
answers.C: Deep neural network debugging with manual feature drop
answers.D: LIME analysis without bias metrics

explanation: Clarify’s bias metrics and dashboards directly identify and quantify group disparities.

stem: A supply chain optimization model is highly accurate but opaque. You need feature-level transparency and robust version control. Which workflow fits?

answers.A: Deploy as AWS Lambda with ad-hoc logging
answers.B: Serve via SageMaker Endpoint and inspect output only
answers.C: Use SageMaker Projects with Model Registry and Clarify explainability
answers.D: Export model to S3 and analyze in external notebook

explanation: SageMaker Projects plus Model Registry provides traceability and Clarify offers feature insights.

stem: A marketing team wants to understand why language generation prompts produce certain outputs. You need an explainable approach without exposing model internals. What do you implement?

answers.A: Visualize transformer attention heads
answers.B: Extract embeddings for manual inspection
answers.C: Run explainability only on input tokens
answers.D: Generate attribution maps via integrated gradients API

explanation: Integrated gradients gives token-level attribution without model internals exposure.

stem: An LLM-based chatbot must cite source documents to be explainable. Which AWS service and feature support this?

answers.A: Amazon Lex with sentiment analysis
answers.B: SageMaker JumpStart with default prompts
answers.C: Comprehend for entity extraction
answers.D: Amazon Bedrock with Retrieval Augmented Generation

explanation: Bedrock RAG includes provenance to cite source documents in responses.

stem: You need to compare performance vs interpretability trade-offs across models. Which practice follows human-centered design?

answers.A: Automatically pick highest accuracy model
answers.B: Use the most interpretable regardless of performance
answers.C: Conduct user studies on prototype explanations and refine
answers.D: Deploy all models in parallel without feedback

explanation: User studies ensure explanations meet user needs and inform trade-offs.

stem: An AI ethics team requires documentation of model decision logic. Which artifact from SageMaker fulfills this?

answers.A: Training job CloudWatch logs
answers.B: Model Card with transparency and test results
answers.C: Endpoint invocation metrics
answers.D: S3 bucket lifecycle policy

explanation: Model Cards include decision logic, evaluation results, and transparency details.

stem: A chatbot integrates multiple foundation models. You need a unified explainability layer without custom code. What do you choose?

answers.A: Amazon Q for aggregated query provenance
answers.B: Bedrock Agents without explainability
answers.C: Lambda orchestration only
answers.D: S3 auditing on each model

explanation: Amazon Q provides a unified explainability interface for multi-model chat applications.

stem: An energy company’s demand forecast model is a black box. They need global interpretability and quantitative feature rankings. Which method and service combination should you apply?

answers.A: Run SHAP summary plots via SageMaker Clarify
answers.B: Inspect first-layer weights in a DNN
answers.C: Use LIME on a single prediction
answers.D: Estimate feature correlation externally

explanation: Clarify’s SHAP summary provides global importance rankings across the dataset.

stem: A company deploys a SageMaker real-time inference endpoint in a VPC to serve sensitive PII. The security team requires that all network traffic between on-premises clients and the endpoint never traverse the public internet, and all traffic must be encrypted. Which combination of AWS features meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Use AWS Direct Connect between on-premises and the VPC, and configure a SageMaker VPC endpoint in the VPC; enforce TLS in the endpoint configuration.
answers.B: Use the public SageMaker endpoint over TLS and restrict access by IP address in the IAM policy.
answers.C: Place a public Network Load Balancer in front of the endpoint and enforce TLS; restrict client IPs with security groups.
answers.D: Deploy the endpoint in a private subnet with no internet gateway; use a NAT gateway for egress; require a client VPN.

explanation: A Direct Connect + VPC endpoint ensures traffic never leaves the AWS network. End-to-end TLS in the endpoint config provides encryption. Alternatives either traverse the internet or add unnecessary components.

stem: An organization stores AI training data in an S3 bucket. They must detect accidental public exposure of sensitive data, including PII, as soon as possible. Which solution provides automated detection and alerting for public or compromised bucket objects?

answers.A: Enable S3 Server Access Logging and analyze logs with a custom Lambda function.
answers.B: Use AWS Config rule s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited to trigger SNS notifications.
answers.C: Enable Amazon Macie to continuously monitor the bucket for public access and PII, and configure Macie alerts to Amazon Security Hub.
answers.D: Use CloudTrail Data events for S3 and query with Athena daily for public object ACLs.

explanation: Macie continuously profiles S3 for sensitive data and public access. While AWS Config detects policy changes, it doesn’t inspect object content; log analysis is slower and less accurate.

stem: Your team implements an ECR repository for Docker images used in AI workloads. They must automatically scan images for CVEs and receive prioritized remediation recommendations. Which AWS feature should they enable?

answers.A: Enable AWS Config rule ecr-image-tag-mutability to require immutable tags.
answers.B: Enable Amazon Inspector image scanning on ECR for scan-on-push and send findings to Security Hub.
answers.C: Use ECR lifecycle policies to expire untagged images and rely on third-party scanners.
answers.D: Configure GuardDuty to analyze ECR image traffic for anomalies.

explanation: Amazon Inspector’s ECR image scanning provides CVE detection on push and integrates with Security Hub. Config rules manage mutability but don’t scan for vulnerabilities.

stem: A regulated healthcare application trains NLP models on medical records. The team must track data lineage and model changes for audit. Which AWS service combination provides automatic lineage capture of datasets, processing jobs, and model versions?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Experiments and the SageMaker Model Registry to record input datasets, training jobs, and model versions.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Glue Data Catalog for lineage and use CloudWatch Logs for training job events.
answers.C: Use AWS Config to track SageMaker resources and AWS X-Ray for job traces.
answers.D: Implement AWS Step Functions for pipeline orchestration and log parameters to CloudTrail.

explanation: SageMaker Experiments captures lineage of datasets, training jobs and parameters. Model Registry tracks versioning. Glue and Config don’t capture full ML pipeline lineage automatically.

stem: A security audit discovered that your SageMaker notebook instances can download any internet asset because they are in a public subnet. The audit requires blocking internet access while still allowing package installations from approved AWS sources. Which VPC configuration meets these requirements with minimal changes?

answers.A: Move notebooks to private subnets with no route to an Internet Gateway.
answers.B: Keep public subnet but remove the Internet Gateway; traffic will fail.
answers.C: Add a NAT Gateway in an isolated subnet and force all notebook traffic through it.
answers.D: Move notebooks to private subnet with a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and Amazon ECR, and no Internet Gateway.

explanation: Private subnet plus S3 and ECR endpoints allows package installs from approved repos stored in S3/ECR while blocking all other internet egress without a NAT or IGW.

stem: Your AI application uses AWS Lambda functions to preprocess data stored in S3. The security team wants to ensure logs from these functions cannot be tampered with or deleted after 90 days. Which combination of services enforces log immutability?

answers.A: Configure Lambda to write logs to a custom S3 bucket and enable versioning.
answers.B: Route Lambda logs to CloudWatch Logs, set a retention period of 90 days, and rely on CloudTrail for API logs.
answers.C: Route Lambda logs to CloudWatch Logs, export to an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode and a 90-day retention.
answers.D: Send Lambda logs to Kinesis Data Stream and store to DynamoDB with TTL of 90 days.

explanation: CloudWatch Logs export to S3 with Object Lock in Compliance mode prevents deletion or modification for the retention period. Versioning alone is insufficient.

stem: A data scientist must ensure that every step of the model training pipeline is logged and that logs cannot be retroactively modified. Which configuration satisfies this requirement?

answers.A: Enable CloudTrail data events for S3, SageMaker, and KMS; send CloudTrail logs to an S3 bucket with Object Lock in Compliance mode.
answers.B: Use SageMaker Studio built-in logging and rely on CloudWatch Logs retention settings.
answers.C: Configure CloudWatch Logs with a 90-day retention period and encrypt logs with an AWS owned CMK.
answers.D: Export CloudWatch Logs to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to an Elasticsearch cluster.

explanation: CloudTrail data events record every API call; Object Lock ensures logs can’t be altered. CloudWatch retention doesn’t prevent log tampering.

stem: An AI analytics team needs to share S3 training data with another AWS account securely, without exposing data publicly. They also need audit trails of every access. Which combination of features should they implement?

answers.A: Use S3 bucket policy with AWSOrgPrincipal to allow the other account and enable S3 Access Logs.
answers.B: Create an S3 Access Point with cross-account policy for the specific account and enable AWS CloudTrail data events for object reads.
answers.C: Generate pre-signed URLs and distribute them; rely on S3 Server Access Logging.
answers.D: Use S3 replication to the other account bucket; enable CloudWatch metrics.

explanation: S3 Access Points with cross-account policies scope access; CloudTrail data events record each read. Pre-signed URLs can leak; replication duplicates data.

stem: Your model training code pulls data from a private S3 bucket. To protect credentials, you want the SageMaker execution role to retrieve encrypted credentials at runtime. Which combination meets best practice for secrets management?

answers.A: Store credentials as plaintext in S3 encrypted with SSE-S3; grant SageMaker access.
answers.B: Hard-code credentials in the training container and restrict IAM policies.
answers.C: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString and a Lambda to fetch at training start.
answers.D: Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; allow the SageMaker role to retrieve secrets via Secrets Manager API.

explanation: Secrets Manager provides encryption at rest, automatic rotation, and fine-grained access via IAM. Parameter Store also works but Secrets Manager is recommended for credentials.

stem: A security requirement mandates that all SageMaker model artifact S3 buckets must enforce encryption at rest and deny uploads without encryption. Which bucket policy accomplishes this?

answers.A: A Deny statement on s3:PutObject where s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is null.
answers.B: A Deny statement on s3:PutObject if aws:SecureTransport is false.
answers.C: A Deny statement on s3:GetObject where the SSE algorithm is not aws:kms.
answers.D: A Deny statement on s3:DeleteObject if the object is unencrypted.

explanation: Denying PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing enforces encryption at rest. SecureTransport relates to in-transit encryption.

stem: A threat model identifies that SageMaker Notebook instance metadata endpoint could expose IAM credentials. You must prevent notebooks from calling instance metadata. How can you enforce this without code changes?

answers.A: Disable the metadata service on the instance via user data script.
answers.B: Apply an IAM policy denying ec2:DescribeInstanceMetadata for the notebook role.
answers.C: Use an IAM instance profile with ec2:MetadataHttpTokens=required and enforce IMDSv2 only via the launch configuration.
answers.D: Deploy the notebook in a Fargate container that has no metadata endpoint.

explanation: Requiring IMDSv2 with enforced tokens prevents unauthorized metadata access. IAM policies cannot restrict metadata access directly.

stem: Your regression model writes output to a DynamoDB table. The security team mandates encrypted data in transit, encrypted at rest with a customer-managed key, and real-time audit of table operations. Which configuration satisfies all requirements?

answers.A: Enable DynamoDB encryption at rest with AWS owned CMK and configure TLS in the SDK; use CloudWatch metrics.
answers.B: Use a DynamoDB global table for cross-region, enable SSE-KMS with a CMK, and export to CloudTrail.
answers.C: Configure DynamoDB with SSE-C and require HTTPS; enable DynamoDB Streams for auditing.
answers.D: Enable DynamoDB SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK, enforce HTTPS in IAM policy by aws:SecureTransport, and enable CloudTrail data events for the table.

explanation: A CMK gives at-rest control; SecureTransport enforces TLS; CloudTrail data events audit all PutItem/GetItem calls in real time.

stem: When deploying a multi-model SageMaker endpoint, you want to prevent unauthorized model copies or downloads from the endpoint container. Which configuration provides this protection?

answers.A: Deploy the endpoint in a private subnet with no outbound internet.
answers.B: Use a VPC endpoint to restrict container ECR pull traffic.
answers.C: Disable IAM role for the endpoint and use access keys instead.
answers.D: Use an endpoint execution role with Allow pulls from ECR repository only, no S3 or SSM permissions.

explanation: Restricting the execution role to only ECR pull permissions prevents the container from accessing S3 or other services to copy or download model artifacts.

stem: Your AI application uses an Amazon DynamoDB table to store model metadata. The security team requires that table backups must be encrypted with a separate key from the primary table encryption. How do you configure this?

answers.A: Enable point-in-time recovery; it uses same table CMK by default.
answers.B: Use on-demand backups with a separate KMS key specified for backup encryption.
answers.C: Export the table to S3 and apply SSE-C encryption.
answers.D: Use continuous backups to another DynamoDB table encrypted with its own CMK.

explanation: On-demand backups allow specifying a different CMK for backup encryption. PITR uses the table key and cannot be changed.

stem: Your SageMaker inference endpoint uses HTTPS. The security team wants to rotate the TLS certificate every 90 days without downtime. Which solution achieves this with minimal changes?

answers.A: Deploy the endpoint behind an Application Load Balancer with ACM-managed certificates and rotate certificates periodically.
answers.B: Store certificates in S3 and update the endpoint config with CLI on rotation.
answers.C: Use CloudFront with self-managed certificate and swap distributions.
answers.D: Use API Gateway (REST) integration with SageMaker and enable custom domain with ACM-managed certificate, auto-renewed.

explanation: API Gateway custom domain with ACM auto-issues and renews certificates. No downtime occurs and no manual rotation is needed. ALB could work but adds complexity.

stem: A regulated financial services firm deploys an AI model on Amazon SageMaker to process sensitive loan applications. To demonstrate compliance with ISO 27001 and SOC 2, they must provide evidence of model invocation logs, resource configuration drift, and change history across the AI environment. Which AWS service should they use to aggregate and automate the evidence collection for audits?

answers.A: AWS CloudTrail
answers.B: AWS Config
answers.C: AWS Audit Manager
answers.D: AWS Artifact

explanation: AWS Audit Manager automates collection of evidence (from CloudTrail, Config, etc.) and maps it to frameworks like ISO 27001 and SOC 2. CloudTrail and Config alone store logs and configurations but don’t automate audit evidence collection. Artifact provides compliance documents, not operational evidence.

stem: A healthcare startup uses AI to categorize patient imaging data. They must implement data retention policies to comply with a 7-year medical record retention law and ensure no deletions before that period. Which combination of features enforces this requirement at the storage layer?

answers.A: Amazon S3 Lifecycle rule transitioning objects to Glacier after 7 years
answers.B: Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a 7-year retention period
answers.C: S3 Versioning enabled with manual deletion controls
answers.D: AWS Backup vault locks for S3 with a 7-year lock period

explanation: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode enforces retention periods (immutable) and prevents deletion before expiry. Lifecycle rules alone cannot prevent deletion. Versioning doesn’t enforce retention, and AWS Backup doesn’t support S3 object lock at source.

stem: A multinational AI company must comply with data sovereignty laws requiring that model training data and logs for EU-based customers never leave EU regions. Which approach enforces this at the account level?

answers.A: Use AWS Organizations Service Control Policy to restrict resource creation to EU regions
answers.B: Enable AWS Config Multi-Region recording only for EU regions
answers.C: Set S3 bucket policies to deny non-EU region replication
answers.D: Use IAM permissions to limit access based on AWS region tag

explanation: A Service Control Policy (SCP) can block any creation of resources outside specified regions across accounts. Config recording and bucket policies address logging and replication but don’t prevent resource creation globally. IAM region tags can be bypassed if misconfigured.

stem: A gaming company uses a foundation model via Amazon Bedrock. They need to ensure all prompts and responses are logged and retained for auditing, while minimizing administrative overhead. Which feature should they enable?

answers.A: Bedrock Fine-tuning with S3 logging
answers.B: Enable CloudTrail Data Events for Bedrock
answers.C: Use Bedrock API Gateway with CloudWatch logs
answers.D: Enable Amazon Bedrock Activity Logging to Amazon S3

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Activity Logging delivers prompts and model responses directly to S3 for auditing. CloudTrail doesn’t natively capture Bedrock payloads. API Gateway with CloudWatch adds complexity and may not log responses.

stem: A biotech firm must ensure that cryptographic keys used by its AI workloads comply with rotation policies mandated by NIST 800-57. They also need to record each rotation event for audits. Which configuration satisfies both requirements?

answers.A: AWS KMS automatic key rotation enabled and AWS CloudTrail logging of KMS key usage events
answers.B: Manual KMS key rotation every 90 days and SNS notifications
answers.C: Store keys in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation schedule and CloudWatch Logs
answers.D: Use KMS Customer-Managed Keys without rotation and document rotations manually

explanation: KMS automatic key rotation meets NIST’s rotation requirement. CloudTrail logs each key usage and rotation event for audits. Secrets Manager is for secrets, not KMS keys. Manual rotation and manual documentation are prone to error.

stem: A government agency requires proof that all data classification labels applied to AI training datasets are consistently enforced at access time and logged for audit. Which AWS feature combination accomplishes this?

answers.A: AWS Macie classification jobs with CloudWatch Logs
answers.B: AWS Lake Formation tag-based access control with CloudTrail logging
answers.C: S3 bucket policies using object tags with Config rules
answers.D: AWS Glue Data Catalog tags with Athena access logs

explanation: Lake Formation tag-based access control enforces classification labels at query/run time and CloudTrail logs access attempts and policy evaluations. Macie only classifies data, not enforce. S3 policies and Glue tags don’t provide unified enforcement with audit logging across services.

stem: A retail AI application must maintain governance documentation for all third-party AI model licensing across its organization. They need to store model license documents, track approval status, and make them available for compliance reviews. Which AWS service combination is most appropriate?

answers.A: AWS Artifact for storing compliance documents and AWS Service Catalog for approval workflows
answers.B: AWS License Manager for AI model licenses and AWS Config for tracking
answers.C: Amazon S3 with Inventory and AWS IAM for access control
answers.D: AWS Secrets Manager for document storage and AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store

explanation: AWS Artifact provides storage and retrieval of compliance/licensing documents, while Service Catalog can manage approval workflows for model usage. License Manager is for software licenses, not documents. S3/inventory doesn’t provide workflows. Secrets Manager and Parameter Store aren’t suited for documents.

stem: A healthcare AI solution must ensure that model explainability artifacts (e.g., SHAP values) are retained for at least three years and accessible for audits. They also need to track who accessed these artifacts. Which approach satisfies both requirements?

answers.A: Store artifacts in S3 with access logging enabled and Object Lock with 3-year retention
answers.B: Publish artifacts to AWS Glue Data Catalog with 3-year lifecycle
answers.C: Save artifacts in DynamoDB with PITR and CloudWatch Logs
answers.D: Use AWS RDS with automated backups and IAM auditing

explanation: S3 with Object Lock in Compliance mode ensures retention. S3 access logging records who accessed artifacts. Glue Catalog doesn’t store artifacts; DynamoDB PITR and CloudWatch Logs don’t provide immutability or direct access logs at file level; RDS backups aren’t suitable for artifact storage.

stem: A global AI service provider must comply with multiple regulatory frameworks (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS) and present a unified compliance dashboard. Which AWS service can consolidate evidence from multiple sources and provide framework-based status?

answers.A: AWS Security Hub
answers.B: AWS Config dashboard
answers.C: AWS Audit Manager
answers.D: AWS Well-Architected Tool

explanation: Audit Manager maps evidence from CloudTrail, Config, IAM, etc., to multiple compliance frameworks and provides a unified dashboard. Security Hub focuses on security findings, Config dashboards show resource compliance, and Well-Architected Tool is for architecture reviews.

stem: A global healthcare company uses AI to process patient data. They need to enforce that all AI-related API calls originate from within their VPC and that any violations are captured for audit. Which configuration meets this need?

answers.A: Use AWS WAF to block external calls and CloudWatch alarms
answers.B: Require TLS mutual authentication and log to CloudTrail
answers.C: Deploy VPC Interface endpoints for AI services and enable CloudTrail for AWS PrivateLink logs
answers.D: Use Security Groups to restrict IPs and S3 bucket policies

explanation: VPC interface endpoints (PrivateLink) ensure API calls stay within VPC; CloudTrail logs PrivateLink calls for audit. WAF is for HTTP endpoints, mutual TLS doesn’t enforce VPC origin, security groups and bucket policies don’t cover all AI service APIs.

stem: A fintech company’s risk committee requires that any change to AI-model hyperparameters in production must be approved and logged. They also want to recover the previous approved hyperparameters if needed. What solution provides this capability?

answers.A: Use SageMaker Model Registry with approval workflows and version tracking
answers.B: Store hyperparameters in AWS Secrets Manager with version labels
answers.C: Log hyperparameter changes via CloudWatch and manual approval
answers.D: Maintain hyperparameters in DynamoDB with PITR

explanation: Model Registry supports model versions, approval statuses, and metadata including hyperparameters. It allows rollback to prior versions. Secrets Manager isn’t designed for hyperparameter metadata and approvals. CloudWatch logs are not structured for governance; DynamoDB PITR captures data but lacks approval workflows.

stem: An AI company must implement data residency enforcement for model inference logs, ensuring logs for APAC customers are stored only in APAC regions. Which mechanism enforces this and prevents misconfiguration?

answers.A: CloudTrail multi-region trails with S3 replication restrictions
answers.B: Use IAM conditions to restrict bucket ARNs by region
answers.C: AWS Organizations SCP denying log delivery outside specified APAC regions
answers.D: AWS Config rule to detect cross-region log buckets

explanation: An SCP can block any S3 log delivery to buckets outside allowed regions at organization level. Config rules detect misconfig but don’t prevent creation. IAM conditions can be bypassed if incorrect policy applied. CloudTrail replication restrictions aren’t a feature.

stem: An online recommendation service updates user suggestions instantly as users browse items. Which inferencing type best describes this system?

answers.A: Batch inferencing
answers.B: Real-time inferencing
answers.C: Offline inferencing
answers.D: Mini-batch inferencing

explanation: Instant updates require real-time inferencing, not periodic batch processing.

stem: A model achieves 98% accuracy on training data but only 60% on validation data. This pattern indicates:

answers.A: Underfitting
answers.B: Overfitting
answers.C: Good fit
answers.D: Data bias

explanation: High training and low validation accuracy show the model memorized training data (overfitting).

stem: A retailer has transactional logs without labels and wants to segment customers by purchase behavior. Which learning approach is most appropriate?

answers.A: Supervised learning
answers.B: Unsupervised learning
answers.C: Reinforcement learning
answers.D: Deep learning

explanation: Clustering segments without labels requires unsupervised learning.

stem: In machine learning, the iterative process that adjusts weights during model training is called the “algorithm,” whereas the learned weights themselves constitute the “”:

answers.A: Model
answers.B: Feature
answers.C: Dataset
answers.D: Payload

explanation: The algorithm is the procedure; the model is the learned representation (weights).

stem: A monthly invoice processing pipeline processes transactions at month end. What type of inferencing does it use?

answers.A: Real-time inferencing
answers.B: Online inferencing
answers.C: Batch inferencing
answers.D: Stream inferencing

explanation: Processing data at set intervals is batch inferencing.

stem: A model with multiple hidden layers that learns hierarchical feature representations is best described as:

answers.A: Machine learning model
answers.B: Deep learning model
answers.C: Reinforcement learning model
answers.D: Statistical model

explanation: Multiple hidden layers characterize a deep learning model.

stem: A robotic arm learns to sort objects by trial and error with a reward for correct sorting. This exemplifies:

answers.A: Supervised learning
answers.B: Unsupervised learning
answers.C: Reinforcement learning
answers.D: Transfer learning

explanation: Learning via rewards/punishments is reinforcement learning.

stem: A marketing team uses a pre-trained model with billions of parameters on text corpora to generate summaries. This model type is known as:

answers.A: Small language model
answers.B: Large Language Model (LLM)
answers.C: Rule-based model
answers.D: Reinforcement model

explanation: Models with billions of parameters trained on text are Large Language Models.

stem: Image files used in computer vision tasks are best characterized as which data type?

answers.A: Structured data
answers.B: Unstructured data
answers.C: Tabular data
answers.D: Categorical data

explanation: Image pixels do not follow fixed schema—hence unstructured.

stem: In linear regression, the linear equation y=mx+b with learned m and b represents the:

answers.A: Model
answers.B: Algorithm
answers.C: Feature
answers.D: Weight

explanation: The equation with learned parameters is the model; algorithm is how it’s learned.

stem: A telecom company wants to group customers based on usage patterns without prior labels. Which technique and learning type apply?

answers.A: Supervised classification
answers.B: Unsupervised clustering
answers.C: Supervised regression
answers.D: Reinforcement Q-learning

explanation: Grouping without labels uses unsupervised clustering.

stem: A delivery drone optimizes its navigation policy by trial and error with reward for timely delivery. Which learning type and business objective does this exemplify?

answers.A: Supervised learning for prediction
answers.B: Unsupervised learning for segmentation
answers.C: Reinforcement learning for decision optimization
answers.D: Deep learning for feature extraction

explanation: Using rewards to improve decisions is reinforcement learning for decision optimization.

stem: An autonomous vehicle collects LIDAR point clouds in real time but processes them hourly for route refinement. Identify the data type and inferencing mode.

answers.A: Time-series & real-time
answers.B: Unstructured & batch
answers.C: Structured & streaming
answers.D: Tabular & real-time

explanation: Point clouds are unstructured; hourly processing is batch inferencing.

stem: DeepMind’s AlphaGo learns to win Go by playing games against itself and receiving rewards. Which learning paradigm is this?

answers.A: Supervised learning
answers.B: Unsupervised learning
answers.C: Reinforcement learning
answers.D: Transfer learning

explanation: Self-play with rewards is a reinforcement learning approach.

stem: In a sentiment analysis pipeline, converting word indices into dense vectors is called:

answers.A: Tokenization
answers.B: Embedding
answers.C: Chunking
answers.D: Sampling

explanation: Embedding maps discrete indices to continuous vectors.

stem: A bank predicts the likelihood of loan default as a probability. Which ML task is this?

answers.A: Classification
answers.B: Regression
answers.C: Clustering
answers.D: Dimensionality reduction

explanation: Predicting discrete outcome probabilities is classification.

stem: An email spam filter learns from labeled spam and non-spam examples. Identify the data labeling and learning type combination.

answers.A: Labeled data & supervised learning
answers.B: Unlabeled data & unsupervised learning
answers.C: Labeled data & reinforcement learning
answers.D: Unstructured data & supervised learning

explanation: Spam filters use labeled examples for supervised learning.

stem: An autoencoder learns normal transaction patterns without labels to detect anomalies. This technique falls under:

answers.A: Unsupervised learning
answers.B: Supervised learning
answers.C: Reinforcement learning
answers.D: Transfer learning

explanation: Autoencoders train on unlabeled data to learn patterns—unsupervised learning.

stem: A fraud detection system predicts fraudulent transactions instantly using a trained supervised model. Which combination applies?

answers.A: Unsupervised learning & batch inferencing
answers.B: Supervised learning & batch inferencing
answers.C: Supervised learning & real-time inferencing
answers.D: Reinforcement learning & real-time inferencing

explanation: Predicting fraud instantly with a trained supervised model is real-time inferencing.

stem: A customer segmentation model groups users on the fly into clusters for personalized offers. Which combination applies?

answers.A: Supervised learning & real-time
answers.B: Unsupervised learning & real-time
answers.C: Supervised learning & batch
answers.D: Reinforcement learning & batch

explanation: On-the-fly grouping without labels is unsupervised real-time inferencing.

stem: Gradient descent, used to minimize loss during training, is an example of a:

answers.A: Model
answers.B: Algorithm
answers.C: Feature
answers.D: Hyperparameter

explanation: Gradient descent is the algorithm that updates model parameters.

stem: In a text-to-speech system, converting written language into spoken audio falls under which AI subdomain?

answers.A: Computer vision
answers.B: Natural language processing
answers.C: Reinforcement learning
answers.D: Anomaly detection

explanation: Text-to-speech processes language, an NLP task.

stem: A financial institution must flag potentially fraudulent credit card transactions in real time. Which ML technique is most appropriate to minimize false negatives while allowing probabilistic scoring?

answers.A: Logistic regression with threshold tuning
answers.B: K-means clustering with centroid distance
answers.C: Principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction
answers.D: Linear regression predicting fraud score

explanation: Fraud detection is a supervised, binary classification problem. Logistic regression provides probabilistic outputs and can be threshold-tuned to balance false positives/negatives. Clustering and PCA are unsupervised and linear regression predicts continuous values, not classes.

stem: An e-commerce retailer wants to segment customers for targeted marketing using only purchase history without labels. Which ML technique should they apply?

answers.A: Hierarchical or k-means clustering
answers.B: Decision tree classification
answers.C: Logistic regression
answers.D: Reinforcement learning

explanation: Customer segmentation without labels is an unsupervised clustering problem. Classification and regression require labeled outcomes; reinforcement learning is for action policies, not segmentation.

stem: A subscription service wants to predict if a customer will churn at the end of their billing cycle. Which ML approach best matches this requirement?

answers.A: Time-series regression forecasting
answers.B: Supervised classification
answers.C: Unsupervised clustering
answers.D: Reinforcement learning

explanation: Churn prediction is a binary outcome (churn/no churn), so supervised classification is appropriate. Forecasting is for continuous numeric predictions, clustering is unsupervised, and reinforcement learning addresses sequential decision making.

stem: A retail chain needs to forecast next quarter’s sales volume at each store using historical daily sales data. Which ML technique is most suitable?

answers.A: Time-series forecasting
answers.B: Binary classification
answers.C: K-means clustering
answers.D: Anomaly detection

explanation: Sales forecasting over time is a time-series regression problem. Classification and clustering are not designed for predicting continuous values over time; anomaly detection identifies outliers, not future values.

stem: A travel website wants to analyze free-form customer reviews to determine overall sentiment. Which AWS managed service should they choose?

answers.A: Amazon Comprehend
answers.B: Amazon Translate
answers.C: Amazon Lex
answers.D: Amazon Polly

explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides NLP capabilities including sentiment analysis. Translate is for language translation, Lex is for chatbots, and Polly is for text-to-speech.

stem: A call center needs to generate text transcripts from live voice calls for compliance auditing. Which AWS service do you recommend?

answers.A: Amazon Transcribe
answers.B: Amazon Comprehend
answers.C: Amazon Lex
answers.D: Amazon Polly

explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text. Comprehend analyzes text, Lex builds chatbots, and Polly generates speech from text.

stem: A company wants to build an IVR system that understands customer intent and routes calls accordingly. Which service is the best fit?

answers.A: Amazon Lex
answers.B: Amazon Polly
answers.C: Amazon Transcribe
answers.D: Amazon Comprehend

explanation: Amazon Lex provides intent recognition and dialog management ideal for IVR. Polly is TTS, Transcribe is speech-to-text, and Comprehend is NLP analysis not optimized for conversational flows.

stem: An operations team wants to generate spoken alarms from textual alerts. Which AWS service fulfills this without custom model training?

answers.A: Amazon Polly
answers.B: Amazon Lex
answers.C: Amazon Comprehend
answers.D: Amazon Transcribe

explanation: Amazon Polly provides high-quality text-to-speech directly. Lex is for chatbots, Comprehend is text analysis, and Transcribe is speech recognition.

stem: A global marketing team needs to localize ad copy from English to Spanish at scale. Which service will deliver accurate, context-aware translations?

answers.A: Amazon Translate
answers.B: Amazon Comprehend
answers.C: Amazon Polly
answers.D: Amazon Transcribe

explanation: Amazon Translate provides neural machine translation with context awareness. Comprehend analyzes sentiment and entities, Polly is TTS, and Transcribe is STT.

stem: A logistics provider wants to automatically extract line-item details from scanned invoices. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon Textract
answers.B: Amazon Comprehend
answers.C: Amazon Rekognition
answers.D: Amazon Translate

explanation: Amazon Textract extracts structured text (forms, tables) from documents. Comprehend analyzes unstructured text, Rekognition analyzes images, and Translate handles translation.

stem: A social media platform needs to tag objects in user-uploaded photos for content discovery. Which AWS service should be used?

answers.A: Amazon Rekognition
answers.B: Amazon Textract
answers.C: Amazon Comprehend
answers.D: Amazon Translate

explanation: Rekognition provides object and scene detection in images. Textract is OCR, Comprehend is text NLP, and Translate is for language translation.

stem: A small bakery with stable weekly orders wants to plan production without high tooling costs. Which solution is most appropriate?

answers.A: Rule-based heuristic forecasting
answers.B: Time-series ML forecasting
answers.C: Unsupervised clustering
answers.D: Supervised classification

explanation: Low variance and predictable demand can be handled with simple heuristics. ML forecasting adds unnecessary cost and complexity; clustering and classification don’t predict numerical demand.

stem: A startup with only 100 users wants to recommend content. Labels are sparse. Which initial approach maximizes ROI?

answers.A: Rule-based content filtering
answers.B: Deep collaborative filtering
answers.C: Supervised classification
answers.D: Reinforcement learning

explanation: With sparse data and few users, simple rule-based filtering yields ROI. Complex models require more data and expertise and may not outperform basic heuristics initially.

stem: A retail chain has historical sales and external factors; they need to fine-tune a model to predict sales uplift from promotions. Which AWS service covers end-to-end without deep ML coding?

answers.A: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
answers.B: Amazon Personalize
answers.C: Amazon Forecast
answers.D: Amazon Comprehend

explanation: SageMaker Autopilot automates training and tuning with custom data. Forecast is specialized for time-series only, Personalize is for recommendations, and Comprehend is NLP.

stem: A content platform must recommend articles based on user reading history but has no labeled preferences. Which AWS service accelerates this?

answers.A: Amazon Personalize
answers.B: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
answers.C: Amazon Comprehend
answers.D: Amazon Kendra

explanation: Amazon Personalize provides collaborative filtering and content-based recommendations without requiring deep ML expertise. Ground Truth labels data, Comprehend is NLP, and Kendra is enterprise search.

stem: A compliance team needs to automatically detect PII (names, SSNs) in stored S3 objects. Which service fulfills this requirement?

answers.A: Amazon Macie
answers.B: AWS Config
answers.C: Amazon GuardDuty
answers.D: Amazon Macie

explanation: Amazon Macie uses ML to detect PII in S3. Config monitors resources, GuardDuty detects threats, so only Macie fits.

stem: A retailer must decide whether to use ML or rule-based automation for order fraud checks. Which factor indicates ML is NOT appropriate?

answers.A: Large historical dataset available
answers.B: Patterns frequently change
answers.C: High risk of loss on misclassification
answers.D: Business rules are stable and simple

explanation: Stable and well-defined rules don’t justify ML complexity. ML is appropriate when data is large, patterns evolve, and high accuracy is needed.

stem: A media company needs to automatically generate metadata tags (keywords) for video frames. Which service solves both image analysis and metadata extraction without custom training?

answers.A: Amazon Rekognition Video
answers.B: Amazon Comprehend
answers.C: Amazon Translate
answers.D: Amazon Textract

explanation: Rekognition Video provides frame-level object detection and tagging. Comprehend is NLP, Translate translates text, Textract extracts text from images/documents.

stem: A news aggregator wants to deliver personalized article feeds by learning user preferences over time. Which AWS service should be used to avoid building custom ML pipelines?

answers.A: Amazon Personalize
answers.B: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
answers.C: Amazon Comprehend Topics
answers.D: Amazon Forecast

explanation: Amazon Personalize offers managed recommendation models. Ground Truth is labeling, Comprehend Topics is unsupervised grouping, Forecast is time-series.

stem: A vendor needs to translate medical device manuals, preserving domain-specific terminology. Which feature of Amazon Translate helps achieve this?

answers.A: Custom parallel data
answers.B: Custom terminology glossary
answers.C: Neural Text to Speech
answers.D: Active Custom Translation

explanation: Custom terminology glossaries ensure consistent translation of terms. Parallel data can improve quality, but glossaries specifically lock term translations. Neural TTS is Polly; active custom translation isn’t a separate feature.

stem: A retail analytics team needs to perform exploratory data analysis and feature engineering on customer transaction data before model training. They want a visual, low-code tool that integrates with Amazon S3 and writes features directly to a centralized store for reuse. Which AWS service combination should they choose?

answers.A: AWS Glue DataBrew for EDA and Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
answers.B: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler for EDA and Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
answers.C: AWS Glue for EDA and Amazon S3 for feature storage
answers.D: Amazon Athena for EDA and Amazon DynamoDB for feature storage

explanation: Data Wrangler provides visual EDA and preprocessing and natively writes to SageMaker Feature Store, enabling feature reuse.

stem: An online gaming company wants to monitor model performance post-deployment to detect data drift and bias. Which combination of AWS services meets both requirements with minimal custom code?

answers.A: Amazon CloudWatch metrics and Amazon QuickSight dashboards
answers.B: AWS Lambda functions and Amazon SNS alerts
answers.C: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor and Amazon SageMaker Clarify
answers.D: AWS Config rules and AWS CloudTrail logs

explanation: Model Monitor captures data drift, Clarify monitors bias. Together they automate monitoring with minimal code.

stem: A financial services firm needs hyperparameter tuning at scale for their credit-risk classification model. Which SageMaker feature should they use, and why?

answers.A: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning, because it launches parallel training jobs to search hyperparameter space
answers.B: SageMaker Neo, because it compiles models for edge deployment
answers.C: SageMaker Debugger, because it visualizes gradients during training
answers.D: SageMaker Edge Manager, because it manages endpoints at the edge

explanation: Automatic Model Tuning runs parallel training with different hyperparameter sets to optimize a specified metric.

stem: A start-up wants to serve a deep learning inference endpoint with unpredictable traffic patterns and minimize cost. Which production method should they choose?

answers.A: Deploy on Amazon EC2 behind an Application Load Balancer
answers.B: Use SageMaker batch transform with scheduled jobs
answers.C: Host a self-managed Kubernetes cluster with auto-scaling
answers.D: Deploy a SageMaker serverless inference endpoint

explanation: Serverless inference automatically scales to zero and up on demand, minimizing cost under unpredictable traffic.

stem: During model evaluation, the data scientist notices class imbalance. They need a metric that accounts for precision and recall. Which metric should they choose?

answers.A: Accuracy
answers.B: F1 score
answers.C: Mean squared error
answers.D: Log loss

explanation: F1 score combines precision and recall, making it suitable for imbalanced classes.

stem: A marketing team wants reproducible experiments and lineage tracking for each model iteration. Which SageMaker capability should they leverage?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
answers.B: SageMaker Clarify
answers.C: SageMaker Experiments
answers.D: SageMaker Edge Manager

explanation: SageMaker Experiments tracks parameters, metrics, artifacts, and lineage of experiments for reproducibility.

stem: A hospital develops a medical imaging classifier. Regulations require ad-hoc manual review of flagged cases. Which combination helps automate inference and human review?

answers.A: SageMaker batch transform and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms
answers.B: SageMaker real-time endpoint and AWS Lambda
answers.C: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) with SageMaker real-time endpoint
answers.D: SageMaker Neo compiled model and AWS Step Functions

explanation: A2I routing config on SageMaker endpoint sends uncertain predictions for human review automatically.

stem: An e-commerce firm wants to compare performance of a custom model against a pre-trained model from JumpStart without managing training infrastructure. Which approach meets this requirement?

answers.A: Download JumpStart model, fine-tune locally, compare metrics
answers.B: Use SageMaker JumpStart to deploy both models to endpoints and run A/B tests
answers.C: Use Amazon EC2 instances for both models, deploy batch transforms
answers.D: Use AWS Lambda for custom code and AWS Glue for pre-trained inference

explanation: JumpStart can deploy both pre-trained and custom models to endpoints; A/B testing through Invocation and metrics comparison.

stem: A data science team must compare multiple model versions’ performance on a benchmark dataset and register the best version for production. Which workflow accomplishes this?

answers.A: Use AWS Glue jobs to evaluate models and update S3
answers.B: Evaluate in Jupyter notebooks, manually tag models
answers.C: Use SageMaker Experiments for tracking, register in SageMaker Model Registry
answers.D: Deploy all versions to endpoints and pick highest throughput

explanation: Experiments track runs; Model Registry stores approved model versions for production.

stem: A team needs to retrain their fraud detection model when input data distribution changes significantly. Which process should they implement?

answers.A: Use Model Monitor to detect drift and trigger SageMaker Pipelines retraining step
answers.B: Daily manual retraining based on calendar schedule
answers.C: Use CloudWatch to trigger a Lambda every hour for retraining
answers.D: Rebuild model only when accuracy falls below 99%

explanation: Model Monitor detects statistical drift and can trigger Pipelines to automate retraining upon drift detection.

stem: Which SageMaker feature helps ensure model reproducibility by capturing Docker environment, code, data input location, and hyperparameters automatically?

answers.A: SageMaker Clarify
answers.B: SageMaker Experiments
answers.C: SageMaker Model Monitor
answers.D: SageMaker Edge Manager

explanation: Experiments automatically records environment, inputs, parameters, and outputs to reproduce runs exactly.

stem: After deploying a computer vision model to an endpoint, the data science team needs to detect bias toward certain image attributes. Which tool and integration should they use?

answers.A: Use CloudWatch to track accuracy per attribute
answers.B: Use Batch Transform and Athena queries
answers.C: Use QuickSight dashboards on logs
answers.D: Integrate SageMaker Clarify with endpoint data capture

explanation: Clarify can analyze captured prediction data from endpoints to assess bias across attributes.

stem: A healthcare provider must ensure their model pipeline is compliant and records all configuration changes. Which service combination supports compliance and auditing for both data and model steps?

answers.A: SageMaker Model Monitor and GuardDuty
answers.B: AWS CloudTrail with SageMaker Pipeline logging
answers.C: AWS Config and Amazon Inspector
answers.D: Amazon Macie and AWS Key Management Service

explanation: CloudTrail records API calls for pipelines and configurations, ensuring audit trails; pipelines log each step.

stem: A data science team is building a document retrieval system using embeddings. They initially split documents into fixed 512-token chunks with no overlap, resulting in poor semantic coherence at chunk boundaries. Which chunking strategy best improves retrieval quality while controlling embedding count?

answers.A: Keep 512-token fixed chunks and add a 50-token overlap between consecutive chunks.
answers.B: Use sentence-boundary chunking, grouping up to 512 tokens per chunk without splitting sentences.
answers.C: Reduce chunk size to 256 tokens with no overlap to avoid splitting concepts.
answers.D: Increase chunk size to 800 tokens with no overlap to cover full paragraphs.

explanation: Sentence-boundary chunking preserves semantic units and limits embedding count, improving retrieval without unnecessary overlap.

stem: You need to store embeddings for a multi-language knowledge base. Which metric best captures semantic similarity across languages in a shared vector space?

answers.A: Euclidean distance, since it measures absolute difference between vectors.
answers.B: Manhattan distance, because it sums per-dimension differences.
answers.C: Cosine similarity, as it normalizes for vector magnitude and focuses on orientation.
answers.D: Hamming distance, due to binary representation of multilingual tokens.

explanation: Cosine similarity normalizes vector lengths and highlights semantic orientation, critical for cross-language embeddings.

stem: When fine-tuning a foundation model on domain text, you observe that rare domain tokens are tokenized into multiple subwords, harming learning. Which tokenization change addresses this?

answers.A: Train a custom byte-pair encoding tokenizer including domain vocabulary.
answers.B: Switch to character-level tokenization to avoid subwords.
answers.C: Increase context window size so subwords span longer sequences.
answers.D: Use word-level tokenization to treat each word as a token.

explanation: Custom BPE with domain terms as tokens ensures rare domain words are single tokens, improving model learning.

stem: A team is comparing transformer and diffusion models for image generation. They need rapid, deterministic output for UI previews. Which model type is most appropriate?

answers.A: Transformer-based autoregressive diffusion model for faster, one-shot inference.
answers.B: Standard diffusion model, despite its iterative denoising steps.
answers.C: Variational autoencoder, even though it often blurs details.
answers.D: GAN, because it’s non-iterative but suffers from mode collapse.

explanation: Autoregressive transformer models provide fast, deterministic generation suitable for previews; standard diffusion is iterative.

stem: During prompt engineering you observe model hallucinations when generating code. Which embedding-based approach helps verify correctness?

answers.A: Increase temperature to introduce randomness and explore alternatives.
answers.B: Use larger context windows to feed entire codebase at once.
answers.C: Retrieve relevant code snippets via embeddings and include them as examples in the prompt.
answers.D: Switch to pure instruction-tuned model without retrieval.

explanation: Retrieving similar code via embeddings grounds the model and reduces hallucinations by providing factual examples.

stem: In a multi-modal foundation model, how are image pixels and text tokens aligned in the embedding space?

answers.A: Image CNN features appended to token IDs directly.
answers.B: Project both image and text through modality-specific encoders into a shared vector space.
answers.C: Interleave pixel values and token embeddings in a single sequence.
answers.D: Convert images to text descriptions only and embed as text.
