stem: A company has two AWS Regions that need private, low-latency connectivity. Inter-Region data transfer is 500 GB/month. They want the most cost-effective private connectivity option. Which is correct?

answers.A: AWS Direct Connect with hosted connections in both Regions.
answers.B: Inter-Region VPC peering, routing traffic over the AWS global network without internet traversal.
answers.C: AWS Site-to-Site VPN with Global Accelerator for accelerated private routing.
answers.D: AWS Transit Gateway inter-Region peering with dedicated bandwidth.

explanation: Inter-Region VPC peering routes traffic over the AWS global backbone without internet traversal, providing private low-latency connectivity. Only standard inter-Region data transfer charges apply — no per-hour endpoint fees. Direct Connect requires purchasing connections in each Region with significant monthly port charges — not cost-effective for 500 GB/month. Site-to-Site VPN has per-connection hourly charges plus data transfer. TGW inter-Region peering adds TGW attachment costs ($0.05/hr per attachment) on top of data transfer.

stem: A company uses Route 53 for DNS with 500 million queries per month, primarily internal microservice resolution within VPCs. Which change most reduces Route 53 costs?

answers.A: Migrate all internal DNS queries to Route 53 Resolver endpoints pointing to an on-premises DNS server.
answers.B: Use Route 53 private hosted zones for internal service discovery; private hosted zone query charges are lower than public hosted zone queries.
answers.C: Use AWS Cloud Map for all microservice discovery to avoid Route 53 query charges entirely.
answers.D: Enable Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block unnecessary external queries, reducing total query count.

explanation: Route 53 public hosted zone queries are billed at $0.40 per million; private hosted zone queries are billed at $0.10 per million — a 75% reduction. Moving internal microservice DNS to private hosted zones captures this savings across all internal queries. Route 53 Resolver is already provided for VPC DNS resolution at no additional query charge. Cloud Map uses Route 53 private hosted zones under the hood and adds its own per-instance-hour charges. DNS Firewall blocks malicious queries but doesn't reduce legitimate internal queries.

stem: A company's web application on EC2 behind an ALB is experiencing SQL injection attacks. Which combination of AWS services best protects against this threat with LEAST custom development?

answers.A: Enable VPC Flow Logs and create CloudWatch alarms for suspicious traffic patterns.
answers.B: Deploy AWS WAF with the AWS Managed Rules SQLi rule group attached to the ALB; AWS Shield Standard is automatically enabled.
answers.C: Use Amazon Inspector to scan the application code for SQL injection vulnerabilities.
answers.D: Configure Network ACLs with rate-limiting rules to block IPs sending suspicious requests.

explanation: AWS WAF with managed SQLi rule groups provides immediate, maintained SQL injection protection at the HTTP layer on the ALB. Shield Standard provides automatic DDoS protection at no additional cost. VPC Flow Logs operate at the network layer and cannot inspect HTTP payloads. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities but doesn't block active attacks. NACLs operate at the IP/port layer, not the HTTP application layer.
tags: Threat vectors external to AWS (for example, DDoS, SQL injection)
Integrating AWS services to secure applications (for example, AWS Shield, AWS WAF, IAM Identity Center, AWS Secrets Manager)

stem: A three-tier application has a web tier (public subnets), application tier (private subnets), and RDS database (private subnets). Which security group configuration correctly implements least privilege?

answers.A: Web SG: allow inbound 80/443 from 0.0.0.0/0; App SG: allow inbound 8080 from 0.0.0.0/0; DB SG: allow inbound 5432 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.B: Web SG: allow inbound 80/443 from 0.0.0.0/0; App SG: allow inbound 8080 sourced from the Web SG; DB SG: allow inbound 5432 sourced from the App SG only.
answers.C: All three tiers in one security group allowing ports 80, 443, 8080, and 5432 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.D: Web SG: allow all from 0.0.0.0/0; App SG: allow all from the VPC CIDR; DB SG: allow all from the private subnet CIDR.

explanation: Referencing security groups (not CIDR blocks) in inbound rules ensures each tier only accepts traffic from the tier directly above it. SG references automatically track IP changes. Option A exposes all tiers to the internet. Option C puts all tiers in one SG with public access. Option D allows overly broad access using CIDR ranges, permitting lateral movement between tiers.

stem: A three-tier application has a single RDS MySQL instance as the database tier. The architect must add automatic failover within the same Region with failover time under 2 minutes. What is the simplest solution?

answers.A: Enable RDS Multi-AZ deployment, which synchronously replicates data to a standby instance in a different AZ and automatically fails over via DNS CNAME update.
answers.B: Create daily RDS snapshots and restore to a new instance within 2 minutes if the primary fails.
answers.C: Add an RDS Read Replica in a different AZ and promote it manually if the primary instance fails.
answers.D: Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of RDS to reduce load and improve availability.

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different AZ. Failover is automatic — AWS detects failure and updates the DNS CNAME to point to the standby, typically within 60–120 seconds. No manual intervention required. Snapshot restore takes 20–45+ minutes. Manual replica promotion requires human action and exceeds 2 minutes. ElastiCache reduces database load but doesn't make the database itself highly available.
tags: Identifying metrics based on business requirements to deliver a highly available solution

stem: A company must implement automation to ensure their infrastructure stays in a known-good configuration. Any manual configuration change to EC2 instances must be detected and automatically reverted within 10 minutes. Which solution achieves this?

answers.A: Use Amazon Inspector to scan EC2 instances for configuration drift and alert the security team.
answers.B: Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager with an association that enforces the desired configuration on a schedule every 10 minutes, automatically remediating drift.
answers.C: Enable AWS Config with a custom rule that detects configuration drift and triggers an SNS notification.
answers.D: Use AWS CloudFormation drift detection on a schedule via EventBridge and manually re-apply the stack on drift.

explanation: AWS Systems Manager State Manager continuously enforces a desired configuration state on EC2 instances. Associations run on a configurable schedule (every 10 minutes) and automatically apply the desired configuration, remediating any drift without human intervention. Inspector scans for security vulnerabilities, not general configuration drift. Config with custom rules detects drift but SNS notifications require manual remediation. CloudFormation drift detection identifies drift but remediation requires manual stack re-apply.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
Determining automation strategies to ensure infrastructure integrity

stem: A company runs 12–24 hour Monte Carlo simulations that are fault-tolerant and can be checkpointed. Cost minimization is the primary goal. Which compute option is most appropriate?

answers.A: EC2 Reserved Instances (1-year, compute-optimized) to minimize hourly cost for long-running jobs.
answers.B: AWS Batch with Spot Instance compute environments and job retry configured; checkpoints saved to S3.
answers.C: AWS Lambda with 15-minute maximum execution time, chained via Step Functions for longer jobs.
answers.D: Amazon ECS on Fargate Spot for serverless container execution.

explanation: AWS Batch with Spot Instances provides up to 90% savings versus On-Demand for fault-tolerant compute-intensive workloads. Batch handles job queuing, scheduling, retries on interruption, and Spot fleet management. With S3 checkpointing, interrupted jobs resume rather than restart. Reserved Instances provide savings but not as large as Spot and don't suit variable job schedules. Lambda's 15-minute limit makes 12–24 hour jobs impractical. Fargate Spot is suitable for containerized workloads but per-vCPU/GB pricing is higher than EC2 Spot for long-running jobs.
tags: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
Queuing and messaging concepts (for example, publish/subscribe)

stem: An RDS PostgreSQL instance serves both OLTP workloads and analytics queries. Analytics queries compete with OLTP and cause latency spikes. The team wants to isolate analytics without provisioning a full additional RDS instance. Which solution improves performance with LEAST cost?

answers.A: Create an RDS read replica and direct all analytics queries to the replica, isolating OLTP and analytics workloads.
answers.B: Migrate OLTP to Amazon Aurora and analytics to Amazon Redshift, with DMS replicating between them.
answers.C: Enable RDS Performance Insights to identify and kill long-running analytics queries automatically.
answers.D: Enable RDS Multi-AZ and route analytics queries to the Multi-AZ standby instance.

explanation: An RDS read replica offloads analytics (read-heavy) queries from the OLTP primary instance, isolating the workloads at significantly lower cost than a full RDS instance. Read replicas use asynchronous replication and are suitable for analytics queries that can tolerate slightly stale data. Migrating to Aurora + Redshift is a comprehensive but much more expensive and complex solution. Performance Insights identifies slow queries but cannot enforce workload isolation. The Multi-AZ standby is not accessible for read queries — it is a failover target only.
tags: Configuring read replicas to meet business requirements

answers.B: Warm standby in a second Region with fully scaled application tier
answers.C: Backup and restore with automated snapshots and tested restore runbooks
answers.D: Pilot light with continuously replicated full traffic stack

explanation: The RTO/RPO targets are relatively relaxed, so backup and restore provides the lowest-cost option that still meets objectives when recovery procedures are validated.

stem: An ordering platform runs in one Region and must meet an RTO of 30 minutes and an RPO of 5 minutes after a regional outage. The company wants lower cost than active-active but faster recovery than backup-and-restore. Which disaster recovery strategy should be selected?

answers.A: Backup and restore with nightly snapshots copied to another Region
answers.B: Pilot light with only backups and no continuously replicated databases
answers.C: Warm standby in a secondary Region with scaled-down services and continuous data replication
answers.D: Active-active multi-Region with full production capacity in both Regions

explanation: Warm standby is the best fit for moderate RTO/RPO targets, balancing cost and recovery speed by keeping a minimal but running environment in the secondary Region with replicated data. Backup/restore is too slow, pilot light may not consistently meet 30-minute RTO with this RPO target, and active-active exceeds the stated cost objective.

stem: A global API is hosted in two AWS Regions behind regional Application Load Balancers. Users report variable latency and occasional path-based internet congestion. The company needs faster, more consistent global routing without changing the application. Which option is BEST?

answers.A: Use AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups for both regional ALBs.
answers.B: Place Amazon CloudFront in front of the ALBs and rely on edge caching for dynamic API requests.
answers.C: Use Route 53 simple routing with multiple A records pointing to both ALBs.
answers.D: Create a Site-to-Site VPN from each user location to both Regions.

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves path selection and failover for TCP/UDP applications by using the AWS global network and static anycast IPs. CloudFront helps primarily with cacheable content, Route 53 simple routing does not optimize network path quality, and VPNs are impractical for internet clients at scale.

stem: A research team shares a large S3 dataset with external partners. The company wants partners to pay request and data retrieval charges while retaining bucket ownership and minimizing management overhead. Which configuration should the solutions architect choose?

answers.A: Enable S3 Object Ownership: Bucket owner preferred and bill charges to the bucket owner account.

stem: A stateless web application has a steady baseline load and predictable daily spikes. The team wants to reduce EC2 cost without risking baseline capacity during Spot interruptions. Which purchasing strategy is MOST cost-effective?

stem: A media company must provide artists in a data center with low-latency shared file access to active project files while archiving completed projects cost-effectively for analytics in AWS. The solution must scale as project volume grows. Which architecture is MOST appropriate?

stem: An analytics platform writes millions of small random I/O operations to a database volume and experiences periodic performance spikes. The team needs predictable high performance with the ability to scale storage independently over time. Which option should the architect choose?

answers.A: Use Amazon EBS gp2 volumes and increase EC2 instance size when latency rises.
answers.B: Use Amazon EBS io2 volumes with provisioned IOPS sized for peak demand and expand volume size as needed.

stem: A customer-facing API uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and has sharp daytime traffic peaks with low overnight usage. The business wants to reduce cost without sacrificing performance during peaks. Which change is MOST cost-effective?

answers.C: Migrate to DynamoDB with on-demand mode regardless of relational query requirements.
answers.D: Use a larger Multi-AZ RDS instance to avoid scaling events and simplify operations.

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 can scale capacity with load, reducing idle cost while preserving relational compatibility and peak performance. Extra replicas across Regions increase cost, DynamoDB may not match relational requirements, and permanent overprovisioning with larger RDS instances is inefficient.
tags: Database capacity planning (for example, capacity units)
Determining cost-effective AWS database types (for example, time series format, columnar format)

stem: A private application in Account A must call an internal service hosted behind a Network Load Balancer in Account B. The company wants private connectivity, no public internet path, and minimal data transfer overhead compared with centralized NAT egress. Which approach is BEST?

answers.A: Use an internet-facing ALB in Account B and restrict access by source IP ranges from Account A.
answers.B: Use VPC peering and route all outbound traffic through a shared NAT gateway in Account A.
answers.C: Expose the service through API Gateway edge-optimized endpoints and enforce IAM auth.
answers.D: Publish the service as an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service and consume it through interface VPC endpoints in Account A.

explanation: PrivateLink provides private, scalable network connectivity for cross-account service access without internet exposure, aligning with high-performing and secure network architecture goals. NAT-based paths can add cost and complexity, and internet-facing endpoints do not meet private connectivity requirements.
tags: How to design network architecture (for example, subnet tiers, routing, IP addressing)
Load balancing concepts (for example, Application Load Balancer)

stem: An ecommerce platform currently performs synchronous order processing in a single service, causing failures during traffic bursts. The business needs a loosely coupled architecture that can absorb spikes and continue processing asynchronously. Which design is MOST appropriate?

answers.A: Keep synchronous HTTP calls and scale the monolith vertically during peak periods.
answers.B: Publish order events to Amazon SNS, fan out to SQS queues per downstream service, and process with independent consumers.
answers.C: Store all order events in one RDS table and poll continuously from each service.
answers.D: Send all events directly to AWS Lambda without retries or dead-letter handling.

explanation: SNS with SQS fan-out supports event-driven architectures, queuing and messaging concepts, and decoupled scaling per consumer. Vertical scaling of a monolith or shared polling tables increases coupling, and no-retry Lambda processing is not resilient for bursty workflows.
tags: Queuing and messaging concepts (for example, publish/subscribe)

stem: A startup has several EC2 instances that call S3, DynamoDB, and Secrets Manager. A developer attached a single IAM role with AdministratorAccess to all instances to simplify setup. The security team must remediate this with minimal disruption. Which approach best enforces least privilege?

answers.A: Replace AdministratorAccess with PowerUserAccess, which removes IAM and billing permissions.
answers.B: Create separate IAM roles per service group with only the actions and resources each workload requires, and reassign instance profiles accordingly.
answers.C: Add an SCP to the AWS Organization that denies all actions not on an approved allowlist.
answers.D: Attach a permission boundary to the existing role that restricts it to S3, DynamoDB, and Secrets Manager actions.

explanation: Least privilege means each workload gets only the permissions it needs. Separate roles scoped per workload (and per resource ARN where possible) achieves this. PowerUserAccess is still broadly permissive. SCPs apply organisation-wide and would affect all accounts. A permission boundary on the shared role still grants broad access to every instance regardless of need.
tags: AWS security best practices (for example, the principle of least privilege)
Access controls and management across multiple accounts

stem: A company runs a production workload on Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ. The security team asks who is responsible for patching the underlying operating system of the RDS instances. What is the correct answer?

answers.A: The customer, because they own the database and must apply OS patches via the RDS maintenance window configuration.
answers.B: AWS, because RDS is a managed service and AWS handles OS and database engine patching.
answers.C: Shared: AWS patches the hypervisor; the customer patches the guest OS.
answers.D: The customer must use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply OS patches to RDS instances.

explanation: RDS is a managed database service. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for patching the underlying operating system and the database engine software. The customer is responsible for network access controls, IAM permissions, in-database user management, and data encryption choices. Patch Manager cannot access the RDS underlying OS.
tags: Access controls and management across multiple accounts

stem: A company runs EC2 instances in private subnets that must access S3 buckets. The security policy prohibits any traffic from traversing the public internet, and the solution must not introduce additional per-GB data processing charges. Which solution meets both requirements?

answers.A: Deploy a NAT gateway in a public subnet and route private subnet traffic through it.
answers.B: Create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 and update the private subnet route tables to direct S3 traffic to the endpoint.
answers.C: Create a VPC Interface Endpoint for S3 backed by AWS PrivateLink.
answers.D: Peer the VPC to an AWS-managed S3 VPC and route traffic through the peering connection.

explanation: A Gateway Endpoint for S3 routes traffic from private subnets to S3 over the AWS internal network with no internet traversal and no additional data processing charges. Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for S3 also avoid the internet but incur hourly and data processing charges. NAT gateway routes through the public internet.
tags: Control ports, protocols, and network traffic on AWS

stem: A public API hosted on Amazon API Gateway is experiencing HTTP flood attacks. The security team wants to block requests matching specific URI patterns and rate-limit individual source IPs to 1,000 requests per 5 minutes with minimal latency impact. Which solution achieves this?

answers.A: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the API Gateway stage and configure Shield Response Team (SRT) escalation rules.
answers.B: Associate an AWS WAF Web ACL with the API Gateway stage; add a rate-based rule with a 1,000-request threshold and a regex match rule to block malicious URI patterns.
answers.C: Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of API Gateway and configure connection-rate limiting on the NLB.
answers.D: Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to API Gateway and set CloudFront's default TTL to absorb traffic spikes.

explanation: AWS WAF on API Gateway supports rate-based rules (per IP, per 5 minutes) and string match conditions (regex on URI) to block targeted HTTP floods. Shield Advanced (A) provides DDoS mitigation at the network layer and SRT support but doesn't offer URI-pattern blocking. NLBs don't provide application-layer inspection. CloudFront caching absorbs GET requests but won't block POST floods or specific URI patterns.

stem: A microservices application uses synchronous HTTP calls between services, causing cascading failures when a downstream service is slow. The team wants to decouple services so that a slow consumer does not block producers. Which AWS managed service should be introduced?

answers.A: AWS App Mesh to enforce circuit-breaker patterns between services.
answers.B: Amazon SQS to buffer messages between services; producers write to the queue and consumers poll at their own pace.
answers.C: AWS Step Functions to orchestrate service calls with retry logic.
answers.D: Amazon EventBridge to route synchronous HTTP calls through an event bus.

explanation: SQS decouples producers from consumers by buffering messages. Producers write messages without waiting for consumers; consumers drain the queue at their own pace, absorbing traffic spikes without propagating back-pressure. App Mesh circuit breakers reduce failure propagation but the calls remain synchronous. Step Functions orchestrate workflows but do not decouple real-time produce/consume throughput. EventBridge is an event router, not a queue.
tags: AWS managed services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Transfer Family, Amazon SQS, AWS Secrets Manager)
Using purpose-built AWS services for workloads

stem: A company migrates an application that currently reads configuration from a local config file to AWS. The configuration contains database passwords that must be rotated every 90 days. Multiple EC2 instances need the same configuration. Which AWS managed service provides the best solution with automatic rotation?

answers.A: Store the configuration in an S3 bucket with versioning; update the file on rotation.
answers.B: Use AWS Secrets Manager; store passwords as secrets; enable 90-day rotation; update the application to retrieve secrets via the SDK at startup.
answers.C: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString; write a Lambda function to update the parameter every 90 days.
answers.D: Hard-code credentials in an EC2 launch template and rotate by re-deploying all instances.

explanation: Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation with native Lambda templates for common databases, a managed secret caching layer, and version management. Parameter Store SecureString (C) does not provide automatic rotation natively — it requires a custom Lambda and a separate scheduling mechanism. S3 versioning (A) has no rotation or access-control integration for secrets. Hard-coding credentials is a security anti-pattern.
tags: AWS managed services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Transfer Family, Amazon SQS, AWS Secrets Manager)

stem: A development team is designing a payment processing microservice on Lambda. The service must call a downstream bank API that enforces a maximum of 10 concurrent connections per client IP. Which design pattern best handles this constraint?

answers.A: Set Lambda reserved concurrency to 10 to ensure no more than 10 Lambda instances run simultaneously.
answers.B: Use an SQS queue to buffer payment requests; configure Lambda with an event source mapping and a maximum concurrency of 10 to process the queue.
answers.C: Store bank API credentials in Secrets Manager and share the same connection across all Lambda invocations.
answers.D: Use a Lambda layer with a connection pool library that manages the 10 concurrent connections.

explanation: Lambda functions are stateless and create new connections per invocation. SQS + Lambda with maximum concurrency of 10 ensures no more than 10 Lambda instances (and therefore connections) run at once, while queuing excess requests for later processing. Setting reserved concurrency (A) alone limits concurrency but drops excess invocations rather than queuing them. Lambda layers (D) cannot share connections across separate invocations due to Lambda's stateless execution model.
tags: API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)
Design principles for microservices (for example, stateless workloads compared with stateful workloads)

stem: A company wants to containerise a legacy Java web application currently running on EC2. The team wants minimal changes to the application and a managed container orchestration platform that eliminates EC2 management. Which migration path should the architect recommend?

answers.A: Rewrite the application in a serverless Lambda function and deploy it without containers.
answers.B: Package the application and its JRE into a Docker image; push to Amazon ECR; run on Amazon ECS with Fargate launch type; use an ALB for traffic routing.
answers.C: Install Docker on the existing EC2 instances and run the container manually on each instance.
answers.D: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a Docker platform type; upload a Dockerrun.aws.json manifest.

explanation: ECS on Fargate is the recommended path for containerised workloads with no EC2 management. The application is packaged into a Docker image (minimal changes), pushed to ECR, and run as a Fargate task behind an ALB. Rewriting as Lambda (A) requires significant code changes for a traditional HTTP service. Manual Docker on EC2 (C) still requires EC2 management. Elastic Beanstalk (D) is valid but abstracts less than Fargate and still involves EC2 in some modes.
tags: The orchestration of containers (for example, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)
Workflow orchestration (for example, AWS Step Functions)

stem: A company is evaluating containerisation for its microservices. The operations team has no Kubernetes experience and wants the simplest possible managed container service without managing cluster infrastructure. Which option requires the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Self-managed Kubernetes on EC2 worker nodes.
answers.B: Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type.
answers.C: Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type.
answers.D: Amazon EKS with managed node groups.

explanation: ECS Fargate removes all EC2 and cluster infrastructure management. The team defines task CPU/memory requirements; AWS provisions and manages the underlying compute. EKS with managed nodes (D) still requires understanding Kubernetes concepts. ECS with EC2 launch type (B) requires managing EC2 instances, AMI patches, and cluster capacity. Self-managed Kubernetes (A) has the highest operational overhead.
tags: AWS managed services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Transfer Family, Amazon SQS, AWS Secrets Manager)
API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)

stem: A company needs to build a backend for a mobile app that authenticates users, stores user profiles, and sends push notifications. Traffic is unpredictable but averages 100 requests/day. The team of 2 developers wants to spend as little time as possible on infrastructure. Which architecture best fits?

answers.A: EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB; RDS MySQL; SNS for push notifications.
answers.B: API Gateway + Lambda for REST endpoints; DynamoDB for user profiles; Amazon SNS for push notifications; IAM Identity Center for authentication.
answers.C: API Gateway + Lambda for REST endpoints; DynamoDB for user profiles; Amazon Pinpoint/SNS for push notifications; Amazon Cognito for authentication.
answers.D: ECS Fargate cluster behind an ALB; Aurora Serverless for user profiles; SNS for notifications.

explanation: For a low-traffic mobile backend with a small team, fully serverless is optimal: API Gateway+Lambda (no servers), DynamoDB (no DB admin), Cognito (managed auth for mobile with user pools), SNS/Pinpoint (managed push). EC2+RDS (A) requires server management. IAM Identity Center (B) is for workforce SSO, not end-user mobile auth. ECS Fargate+Aurora Serverless (D) works but adds cluster management overhead.
tags: API creation and management (for example, Amazon API Gateway, REST API)
Serverless technologies and patterns (for example, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda)

stem: A company needs to process real-time sensor data from 10,000 IoT devices, store it for 90 days for analysis, and run ad-hoc SQL queries against it without loading data into a separate data warehouse. Which AWS architecture meets all requirements?

answers.A: Kinesis Data Streams → Lambda → DynamoDB; use DynamoDB PartiQL for SQL queries.
answers.B: Kinesis Data Firehose → S3 (Parquet format, partitioned by date); Amazon Athena for ad-hoc SQL queries on S3 data.
answers.C: Kinesis Data Streams → EC2 fleet → RDS MySQL; use MySQL for ad-hoc queries.
answers.D: IoT Core → SQS → Lambda → Redshift; use Redshift for ad-hoc SQL queries.

explanation: Kinesis Firehose buffers and delivers streaming data to S3 in Parquet format with partitioning for cost-efficient storage. Athena queries S3 data directly using SQL with no data warehouse setup. DynamoDB PartiQL (A) supports SQL-like syntax but is not optimised for analytical aggregations. RDS MySQL (C) requires provisioning and won't scale for 10,000-device sensor data. Redshift (D) works for analytics but adds loading complexity and cost.
tags: Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements
Recommending appropriate compute, storage, networking, and database technologies based on requirements

stem: A company needs to migrate 50 TB of data from their on-premises NAS to Amazon S3. The corporate internet connection is 100 Mbps shared with production traffic. A full transfer would take over 45 days and disrupt production. Which purpose-built AWS service should be used?

answers.A: Use S3 Multipart Upload over the existing internet connection to speed up the transfer.
answers.B: Order an AWS Snowball Edge device; load data offline; ship the device to AWS; AWS imports data to S3.
answers.C: Deploy AWS DataSync over the internet with bandwidth throttling to limit production impact.
answers.D: Use AWS Direct Connect to provision dedicated bandwidth for the migration.

explanation: Snowball Edge is purpose-built for offline bulk data migration when network bandwidth is insufficient. 50 TB over 100 Mbps shared internet would take far too long. Snowball transfers data at 10 Gbps internally and is shipped physically. S3 Multipart Upload (A) still uses the internet connection. DataSync (C) uses the internet and would still take weeks at 100 Mbps. Direct Connect (D) requires weeks to provision and adds ongoing circuit costs.
tags: Using purpose-built AWS services for workloads
How to appropriately use edge accelerators (for example, content delivery network [CDN])

stem: A legal technology company processes thousands of contracts daily. They need to extract key clauses, identify entities (parties, dates, amounts), and classify contract risk — all without custom ML model development. Which combination of AWS managed services covers these requirements?

answers.A: Amazon Textract to extract text from scanned contracts; Amazon Comprehend to identify entities and run custom classification.
answers.B: Amazon Rekognition to scan document images; Amazon Polly to read contracts aloud for review.
answers.C: Amazon Translate to normalise contract language; Amazon Kendra to index and search contracts.
answers.D: AWS Glue to extract contract metadata; Amazon Athena to query extracted fields.

explanation: Textract extracts structured text and tables from scanned PDF contracts. Comprehend identifies entities (names, dates, monetary amounts) and supports custom document classification models — no ML infrastructure required. Rekognition is for image/video analysis, not document text extraction. Translate normalises language but doesn't classify risk. Glue and Athena are ETL and query services for structured data.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)
AWS Managed Services (AMS) with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly)

stem: A media company ingests 10,000 articles per day and needs to automatically categorise them into topics (sports, politics, finance) and detect sentiment for downstream recommendation logic. Which approach requires the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Deploy a custom BERT model on SageMaker endpoints; call endpoints from a Lambda function.
answers.B: Use Amazon Comprehend's built-in topic modelling and sentiment analysis APIs; call from Lambda with no model training.
answers.C: Use Amazon Kendra to index all articles; rely on its built-in FAQ and relevance ranking.
answers.D: Store articles in Elasticsearch; use Elasticsearch ML for categorisation.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides out-of-the-box sentiment analysis and topic modelling without custom model training. Lambda calls Comprehend APIs directly. SageMaker with BERT (A) requires model selection, training, endpoint management. Kendra is an enterprise search service, not a categorisation/sentiment tool. Elasticsearch ML requires cluster management and custom ML pipelines.
tags: Service quotas and throttling (for example, how to configure the service quotas for a workload in a standby environment)
Using AWS services that improve the reliability of legacy applications and applications not built for the cloud (for example, when application changes are not possible)

stem: A company wants to ensure their microservices architecture can handle downstream service failures without cascading. Which distributed design pattern, and which AWS implementation, best achieves this?

answers.A: Saga pattern implemented with AWS Step Functions: compensating transactions roll back state on failure.
answers.B: Circuit Breaker pattern implemented with AWS App Mesh: when a downstream service fails repeatedly, the circuit opens and the calling service returns a fallback response without hammering the failing service.
answers.C: Bulkhead pattern implemented with separate Lambda function concurrency reservations per service.
answers.D: Both B and C: circuit breakers in App Mesh prevent cascade; bulkheads in Lambda prevent one service from exhausting shared concurrency.

explanation: Preventing cascading failures requires multiple patterns. Circuit breakers (App Mesh Envoy) open when downstream error rates exceed a threshold, stopping calls to the failing service. Bulkheads (Lambda reserved concurrency) isolate service concurrency pools so one failing service cannot exhaust Lambda concurrency for others. The Saga pattern (A) handles rollback for distributed transactions, not failure isolation.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A solutions architect needs to determine why 5% of API requests to a Lambda-based service exceed the SLA of 500 ms. X-Ray is enabled. Which X-Ray feature allows the architect to focus only on the slow requests?

answers.A: X-Ray sampling rules: increase the sampling rate to capture 100% of requests.
answers.B: X-Ray Analytics with filter expressions: filter traces where response_time > 500ms to isolate slow requests and identify common subsegments.
answers.C: CloudWatch X-Ray anomaly detection: set an alarm on P99 latency.
answers.D: X-Ray groups: create a group with a filter expression for slow traces; view the group's service map.

explanation: X-Ray Groups allow creating a filtered view of traces using filter expressions (e.g., responsetime > 0.5). The group's service map and analytics show only the slow requests, making it easy to identify bottleneck services. X-Ray Analytics (B) also filters traces but groups provide a persistent, dashboard-level view. Increasing sampling (A) captures more traces but doesn't help isolate slow ones. CloudWatch alarms (C) alert on metrics but don't provide trace-level analysis.
tags: Service quotas and throttling (for example, how to configure the service quotas for a workload in a standby environment)
AWS Managed Services (AMS) with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly)

stem: A company deploys all infrastructure via AWS CloudFormation. A new compliance requirement mandates that all EC2 instances must have specific tags (CostCenter, Environment) at launch. Non-compliant launches must be prevented. Which approach enforces this without requiring code changes to CloudFormation templates?

answers.A: Add an AWS Config rule that checks for required tags; alert the team when tags are missing.
answers.B: Use AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) with a Deny on ec2:RunInstances when the required tag condition keys are absent.
answers.C: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use Lambda to terminate instances launched without required tags.
answers.D: Configure an EC2 launch template with required tags; make it mandatory in the account.

explanation: SCPs can deny ec2:RunInstances calls that lack required tag keys using the aws:RequestTag condition. This is a preventive control at the organisation level — instances simply cannot be launched without the tags. AWS Config (A) is a detective control and does not prevent non-compliant launches. CloudTrail + Lambda (C) terminates after the fact (reactive). Launch templates (D) can pre-fill tags but do not prevent launches without tags via other methods.
tags: AWS global infrastructure (for example, Availability Zones, AWS Regions, Amazon Route 53)

stem: A company's multi-tier application uses a single NAT gateway in one AZ to allow private subnet instances to access the internet. The architecture team identifies this as a SPOF. Which change eliminates it?

answers.A: Create an Elastic IP and associate it with the NAT gateway for a static outbound IP.
answers.B: Deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone; update the route table in each private subnet to use the NAT gateway in the same AZ.
answers.C: Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs.
answers.D: Enable Internet Gateway egress routing for private subnets as a backup path.

explanation: A NAT gateway is AZ-specific. If the AZ hosting the single NAT gateway fails, all private subnets lose internet access. Deploying a NAT gateway per AZ and routing each private subnet's traffic to the local NAT gateway eliminates the SPOF. Elastic IPs (A) don't add redundancy. NAT instances in ASGs (C) are operationally complex compared to NAT gateways. Internet Gateway access from private subnets (D) would expose private instances directly.
tags: Implementing designs to mitigate single points of failure
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company runs a legacy Windows application that cannot be modified but must be made highly available. The application maintains state in local memory and cannot tolerate restarted sessions. Which approach provides the best availability without changing application code?

answers.A: Run two EC2 instances behind an ALB with sticky sessions (session affinity) enabled; enable EC2 Auto Recovery on both instances.
answers.B: Migrate the application to Lambda by rewriting the session state to DynamoDB.
answers.C: Use Amazon AppStream 2.0 to stream the application from a persistent fleet of EC2 instances; AppStream manages instance health and failover.
answers.D: Enable EC2 Auto Recovery; if the instance fails, it is restarted on another host with the same IP.

explanation: Sticky sessions on an ALB route each user to the same EC2 instance, preserving in-memory session state without code changes. Two instances with auto recovery provide redundancy — if one instance fails, recovery restarts it; the other continues serving. Rewriting for Lambda (B) requires significant code changes. AppStream (C) is for streaming desktop apps, not general-purpose web services. Auto Recovery alone (D) doesn't add redundancy; the instance is unavailable during recovery.
tags: Using purpose-built AWS services for workloads
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company builds a message queuing system using a self-managed RabbitMQ cluster on EC2. The cluster requires manual patching, broker configuration, and HA configuration. Which purpose-built AWS service eliminates this management overhead?

answers.A: Amazon SQS Standard Queues: replaces RabbitMQ with a fully managed, highly available queue service.
answers.B: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ: fully managed RabbitMQ broker with built-in HA, patching, and monitoring.
answers.C: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: provides managed message streaming compatible with RabbitMQ clients.
answers.D: AWS Step Functions: orchestrates message workflows without a broker.

explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ provides a managed RabbitMQ broker that is compatible with existing AMQP clients. AWS handles patching, HA configuration, and monitoring. SQS (A) is a different messaging paradigm (not AMQP) and requires client code changes. Kinesis is a streaming service with a different API. Step Functions orchestrates workflows, it is not a message broker.
tags: Using purpose-built AWS services for workloads
AWS Managed Services (AMS) with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly)

stem: A media production company has on-premises editing workstations that require access to a shared file system. Their post-production team needs to move final renders (files 50 GB each) to AWS for distribution. Files must be accessible from the workstations via SMB during production and automatically uploaded to S3 when marked as complete. Which AWS service satisfies this?

answers.A: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server: provides SMB access for editing; use S3 replication to move files to S3.
answers.B: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway: mounts as an SMB share on workstations; files are automatically stored in S3 while a local cache enables fast access.
answers.C: Amazon EFS: provides a shared file system for workstations; use DataSync to copy to S3.
answers.D: Amazon S3 with S3 File Gateway: mount directly on workstations; renders are written to S3 directly.

explanation: Storage Gateway File Gateway is the hybrid solution that presents SMB/NFS locally while transparently writing to S3. The local gateway appliance caches hot data for performance. FSx for Windows (A) provides SMB but is a cloud-only file system, not a hybrid gateway with S3. EFS (C) is NFS-only and not suitable for Windows workstations without NFS client configuration. The Gateway IS the File Gateway (D) — option D repeats B differently but misidentifies the product.
tags: Hybrid storage solutions to meet business requirements
Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands

stem: A company's file storage solution on EFS is currently 10 TB. They expect it to grow to 1 PB over 3 years. They're concerned about capacity planning. Which statement about EFS scaling is correct?

answers.A: EFS has a maximum capacity of 47.9 TiB; they must plan a migration to FSx before reaching that limit.
answers.B: EFS scales automatically to petabytes with no capacity provisioning required; as files are added, storage grows; no user action is needed.
answers.C: EFS requires pre-provisioned throughput and storage; they must request a capacity increase before reaching the current limit.
answers.D: EFS storage scales automatically but throughput must be pre-provisioned in 1 TB increments.

explanation: Amazon EFS is a fully elastic file system that grows and shrinks automatically. There is no pre-provisioning of storage capacity and no maximum capacity limit (designed for petabyte-scale). Throughput scales with storage in the default bursting mode or can be provisioned independently. EFS does not have a 47.9 TiB limit (that was an old EBS limit). Capacity increases are not required.
tags: Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)
Storage types with associated characteristics (for example, object, file, block)

stem: A retail company needs to run computer vision on security camera footage at each of their 500 store locations with sub-second processing latency, even when internet connectivity is intermittent. Which distributed compute approach achieves this?

answers.A: Stream all camera footage to a central AWS region for processing; buffer during outages.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Outposts racks in each store with the inference application; Outposts runs AWS EC2 and ECS services on-premises with local compute, processing footage locally even without internet.
answers.C: Deploy AWS Snowball Edge compute-optimised devices at each store for offline inference.
answers.D: Use AWS IoT Greengrass to deploy the inference model to local gateway devices at each store; inference runs locally on low-power hardware.

explanation: IoT Greengrass deploys Lambda functions and ML models to local edge devices (cameras or gateways) and runs inference locally, eliminating internet dependency and achieving sub-second latency. Outposts racks (B) are data centre solutions — too expensive for 500 retail stores. Snowball Edge (C) is for data migration and occasional edge compute, not continuous real-time inference. Central region processing (A) fails when connectivity is intermittent.
tags: Distributed computing concepts supported by AWS global infrastructure and edge services
AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)

stem: A company runs an in-memory analytics workload that loads 400 GB of data into RAM for processing. The application requires the lowest possible per-GB RAM cost. Which EC2 instance family is most appropriate?

answers.A: C5 (compute optimised): highest vCPU-to-RAM ratio for CPU-intensive analytics.
answers.B: R6g (memory optimised, Graviton): provides high memory-to-CPU ratio at lower cost than x86 memory-optimised instances.
answers.C: T3 (burstable): provides flexible performance at the lowest base cost.
answers.D: I3 (storage optimised): provides NVMe SSD for fast in-memory data access.

explanation: Memory-optimised instances (R, X, z families) provide high RAM-to-vCPU ratios. The R6g (Graviton ARM-based) provides up to 20% better price-performance than equivalent x86 R5 instances. C5 (compute-optimised) has lower RAM per vCPU. T3 burstable instances have limited baseline CPU and low maximum RAM. I3 instances are storage-optimised (NVMe) with moderate RAM.
tags: Scalability capabilities with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, AWS Auto Scaling)
AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)

stem: A company migrates an OLTP database from Oracle to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The Oracle database currently uses 40,000 IOPS for a critical financial application. The team must ensure the RDS instance meets this IOPS requirement. Which EBS volume type and configuration should be selected?

answers.A: gp3 volume: configure throughput and IOPS up to 16,000 IOPS independently from storage size.
answers.B: io2 Block Express volume: configure up to 256,000 IOPS with sub-millisecond latency; suitable for 40,000 IOPS requirement.
answers.C: gp2 volume: size the volume at 40,000 GB to achieve 40,000 IOPS via the 3 IOPS/GB ratio.
answers.D: st1 volume: optimised for sequential I/O with high IOPS for transactional databases.

explanation: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume with sub-millisecond latency, making it suitable for demanding OLTP workloads requiring 40,000 IOPS. gp3 (A) supports a maximum of 16,000 IOPS, insufficient for 40,000. gp2 (C) at 40,000 GB would cost ~$4,000/month for storage alone — impractical. st1 (D) is optimised for sequential throughput (MapReduce, log processing), not transactional IOPS.
tags: Determining an appropriate database type (for example, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)

stem: A company's analytics platform runs complex ad-hoc SQL queries against petabytes of structured data that changes infrequently. Query results are expected within seconds. Which database type is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon DynamoDB: provides single-digit ms latency for ad-hoc queries.
answers.B: Amazon Redshift: columnar data warehouse optimised for complex analytical SQL on petabyte-scale data.
answers.C: Amazon RDS Aurora: relational database optimised for OLTP workloads.
answers.D: Amazon ElastiCache: in-memory database for sub-millisecond query results.

explanation: Redshift is a columnar MPP data warehouse designed for complex SQL analytics over petabytes. Columnar storage means analytical queries scan only the required columns, not entire rows. DynamoDB (A) is a key-value/document store unsuitable for complex ad-hoc SQL aggregations. Aurora (C) is optimised for OLTP transactions, not petabyte analytics. ElastiCache (D) serves pre-computed results from memory, not ad-hoc SQL across petabytes.
tags: Determining an appropriate database type (for example, Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)
Database engines with appropriate use cases (for example, heterogeneous migrations, homogeneous migrations)

stem: An architect is designing the database layer for a multi-tenant SaaS application. Each tenant's data must be isolated, query performance must not degrade as tenants are added, and the cost must scale with tenant count. Which database architecture best meets these requirements?

answers.A: A single RDS PostgreSQL instance with a tenant_id column on every table and row-level security policies.
answers.B: Separate RDS instances per tenant: full isolation but cost scales linearly with tenant count.
answers.C: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with a single database and schema-per-tenant isolation; Aurora Serverless scales compute automatically; schemas provide logical isolation.
answers.D: DynamoDB with tenant_id as the partition key; on-demand capacity scales with actual usage; IAM conditions restrict tenant access.

explanation: DynamoDB with tenant_id as the partition key provides logical data isolation with IAM condition keys for enforcement. On-demand pricing scales precisely with usage. A single RDS instance with row-level security (A) is cost-effective but queries degrade as data grows with many tenants (table bloat). Separate RDS instances (B) provide strong isolation but cost scales linearly and management is complex. Aurora Serverless (C) with schema-per-tenant isolates schemas but performance can degrade under cross-tenant query load.

stem: A VPC has a public subnet and a private subnet. The private subnet's route table has no route to an internet gateway. An EC2 instance in the private subnet needs to download software packages from the internet. Which solution is correct?

answers.A: Add a route 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway in the private subnet route table.
answers.B: Deploy a NAT Gateway in the public subnet, add a route 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway in the private subnet route table.
answers.C: Deploy a NAT Gateway in the private subnet, add a route 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway in the private subnet route table.
answers.D: Enable DNS hostnames on the VPC so the private instance can resolve and reach internet addresses.

explanation: A NAT Gateway must reside in a public subnet (which has a direct route to the IGW). The private subnet route table then has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the NAT Gateway. This allows outbound-only internet access for private instances. Placing the NAT Gateway in the private subnet (C) is invalid — it needs a public subnet to relay traffic. Adding an IGW route to the private subnet (A) makes it a public subnet and exposes the instance directly. DNS hostnames (D) enable DNS resolution but don't provide routing.
tags: Identifying metrics based on business requirements to deliver a highly available solution
Determining the AWS services required to provide a highly available and/or fault-tolerant architecture across AWS Regions or Availability Zones

stem: A company has two VPCs peered together. VPC-A (10.0.0.0/16) and VPC-B (172.16.0.0/16). An instance in VPC-A cannot reach an instance in VPC-B despite the peering connection being active. What is the most likely cause?

answers.A: VPC peering does not support cross-VPC communication between instances.
answers.B: The route tables in both VPCs are missing entries for the peer CIDR ranges pointing to the peering connection.
answers.C: Security groups in both VPCs allow all traffic by default, so the issue is with NACLs blocking traffic.
answers.D: The VPCs have overlapping CIDR ranges, which prevents route table entries from being added.

explanation: A VPC peering connection alone does not route traffic. Route table entries must be manually added in both VPCs: VPC-A needs a route for 172.16.0.0/16 → pcx-xxx, and VPC-B needs a route for 10.0.0.0/16 → pcx-xxx. Security groups also need to allow traffic, but the most common and likely cause of no connectivity with an active peering connection is missing route table entries.
tags: Using AWS services that improve the reliability of legacy applications and applications not built for the cloud (for example, when application changes are not possible)
AWS Managed Services (AMS) with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly)

stem: A serverless application using hundreds of Lambda functions connects directly to an RDS PostgreSQL database. During traffic spikes, the database reports 'too many connections' errors and performance degrades. Which solution best addresses this with minimal application changes?

answers.A: Increase the max_connections parameter on the RDS instance.
answers.B: Add RDS Proxy between Lambda and RDS; configure the Lambda functions to connect via the proxy endpoint.
answers.C: Switch from RDS PostgreSQL to DynamoDB, which has no connection limits.
answers.D: Reduce Lambda concurrency to limit the number of simultaneous database connections.

explanation: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool to RDS and multiplexes thousands of Lambda connections into a small number of persistent database connections. Lambda's function-per-request model creates a new connection for each invocation, which exhausts database connection limits. RDS Proxy is purpose-built for serverless workloads and requires only a connection string change. Increasing max_connections (A) has limits and doesn't solve pooling. DynamoDB (C) requires significant application refactoring. Reducing concurrency (D) throttles the application rather than solving the root cause.
tags: Using purpose-built AWS services for workloads
Proxy concepts (for example, Amazon RDS Proxy)

stem: A company needs to store large video files (each 50 GB) that are uploaded once, accessed frequently for the first 30 days, then rarely accessed. They require 11 nines of durability. Which S3 storage class progression achieves the lowest cost?

answers.A: S3 Standard → S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval via lifecycle policy at 30 days.
answers.B: S3 Standard → S3 Standard-IA via lifecycle policy at 30 days.
answers.C: S3 Reduced Redundancy Storage for all objects.
answers.D: S3 One Zone-IA for all objects to minimize cost.

explanation: S3 Standard provides frequent-access performance and 11 nines of durability. After 30 days, S3 Standard-IA provides the same 11 nines of durability at ~60% lower storage cost with a per-retrieval fee — appropriate for infrequent access. Glacier (A) has retrieval delays (minutes to hours) unsuitable for 'rarely but still accessed' media. Reduced Redundancy (C) provides only 4 nines of durability, violating the requirement. S3 One Zone-IA (D) stores data in one AZ with only 11 nines of durability within that AZ, risking data loss if the AZ fails.
tags: Implementing strategies to ensure the durability and availability of data (for example, backups)
Storage options and characteristics (for example, durability, replication)

stem: A company uses Amazon EFS for shared file storage across EC2 instances in multiple AZs. They need to understand the durability characteristics of EFS. Which statement is correct?

answers.A: EFS stores data in a single AZ with 11 nines of durability.
answers.B: EFS stores data redundantly across multiple AZs within a region, providing 11 nines of durability.
answers.C: EFS stores data on instance-attached NVMe drives, providing high durability through RAID-1 mirroring.
answers.D: EFS durability is equivalent to EBS gp2 volumes: 99.8-99.9%.

explanation: Amazon EFS (Standard storage class) stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones within an AWS Region, providing 11 nines (99.999999999%) of durability. This multi-AZ replication is automatic. EFS One Zone is the exception — it stores data in a single AZ. EFS does not use instance NVMe drives; it's a managed network file system. EBS gp2 durability figures apply to block storage, not EFS.
tags: Storage options and characteristics (for example, durability, replication)
Implementing strategies to ensure the durability and availability of data (for example, backups)

stem: A company wants to query data stored in S3 in Parquet format without loading it into a database. Results must be available within seconds for ad-hoc queries. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon Redshift: load Parquet files into Redshift tables then query with SQL.
answers.B: Amazon Athena: serverless SQL query engine that queries Parquet files in S3 directly, with no infrastructure to manage.
answers.C: Amazon EMR with Apache Spark: run distributed Spark SQL queries against S3 Parquet files.
answers.D: AWS Glue ETL: transform Parquet files to CSV then load into RDS for querying.

explanation: Amazon Athena is purpose-built for serverless, ad-hoc SQL queries directly against S3. It supports Parquet natively and charges per TB scanned. No infrastructure provisioning is required and queries return in seconds. Redshift (A) requires loading data and cluster management. EMR (C) requires cluster provisioning and is more appropriate for large-scale transformation jobs, not quick ad-hoc queries. Glue ETL (D) is a transformation service, not a query service.
tags: Data transformation services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Glue)
Data transfer services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway)

stem: A retail company needs to load daily sales transaction files from on-premises systems into an S3 data lake at midnight each night. The files are up to 500 GB. Which ingestion approach is most operationally simple?

answers.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: stream each transaction as it occurs throughout the day.
answers.B: AWS DataSync scheduled transfer: schedule a nightly DataSync task to copy files from on-premises NFS to S3.
answers.C: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with a Lambda transformation: buffer records and deliver to S3 every hour.
answers.D: Set up an AWS Direct Connect dedicated line and manually scp files using a cron job.

explanation: AWS DataSync is designed for scheduled, large-scale file transfers from on-premises NFS/SMB to S3 (or EFS, FSx). It handles scheduling, encryption in transit, data integrity validation, and bandwidth throttling. For batch/nightly loads, DataSync is operationally simpler than streaming services. Kinesis Data Streams (A) and Firehose (C) are for continuous real-time streaming, not nightly batch file transfers. Manual scp (D) requires infrastructure management and lacks reliability features.
tags: Streaming data services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon Kinesis)

stem: A company continuously syncs data between two S3 buckets in different AWS regions for compliance reasons. They need bidirectional replication with low latency and the ability to handle conflicts. Which S3 feature achieves this?

answers.A: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) configured in both directions with a Lambda function to detect and resolve conflicts.
answers.B: S3 Multi-Region Access Points with S3 Replication: configure two-way replication rules between the buckets.
answers.C: S3 Batch Operations: run a daily job to sync objects between regions.
answers.D: AWS DataSync scheduled task running every 5 minutes to sync both buckets bidirectionally.

explanation: S3 Multi-Region Access Points with bidirectional replication rules support two-way replication between S3 buckets. S3 Replication includes conflict resolution (last-writer-wins based on replication time). One-way CRR (A) with Lambda conflict detection requires custom development and adds latency. S3 Batch Operations (C) are for bulk operations, not continuous sync. DataSync (D) is for on-premises-to-cloud or EFS/FSx transfers, not optimal for S3-to-S3 continuous replication.

Transforming data between formats (for example, .csv to .parquet)

stem: A company needs a shared file system for 20 Linux EC2 instances in the same AZ. The workload is random I/O and requires 3,000 IOPS consistently. They currently use EFS but find it too expensive for this use case. What is a more cost-effective alternative?

answers.A: Use a single EBS Multi-Attach io2 volume attached to all 20 instances simultaneously.
answers.B: Deploy Amazon FSx for Lustre in persistent mode with the required IOPS — FSx for Lustre provides higher performance at lower cost than EFS for IOPS-intensive workloads.
answers.C: Deploy an NFS server on EC2 backed by gp3 EBS volumes and share the NFS mount to all instances.
answers.D: Use EFS with Provisioned Throughput mode at the required level.

explanation: For small-scale shared NFS within a single AZ where full managed-service cost is not justified, a self-managed NFS server on EC2 with gp3 EBS volumes (3,000 IOPS baseline, no additional cost) is the most cost-effective approach. EBS Multi-Attach (A) supports up to 16 instances and requires cluster-aware filesystems — not standard for 20 instances. FSx for Lustre (B) is designed for HPC/ML workloads and isn't cheaper than EFS for general workloads at 3,000 IOPS. EFS Provisioned Throughput (D) charges additionally for provisioned throughput — same service, not cheaper.
tags: Selecting the most cost-effective storage service for a workload
AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)

stem: A media company migrates 500 TB of video assets from on-premises object storage (Swift) to Amazon S3. The existing system uses an HTTP API. Which approach requires the least custom development?

answers.A: Write a Python script using boto3 and the Swift SDK to stream objects from Swift and upload to S3.
answers.B: Use AWS DataSync with a custom agent plugin for Swift-compatible object storage.
answers.C: Use S3 Batch Operations to copy objects in bulk from the Swift endpoint.
answers.D: Contact AWS Professional Services to build a custom migration pipeline.

explanation: For HTTP-based object storage (Swift), a Python script using the Swift SDK to download objects and boto3 to upload to S3 with multipart upload is the most practical approach. DataSync (B) supports NFS, SMB, S3, EFS, FSx, and HDFS — it does not have a native Swift connector. S3 Batch Operations (C) operates on existing S3 objects, not external systems. AWS Professional Services (D) is an option but not 'least custom development' — a simple Python script achieves the same result.

stem: A company runs a memory-intensive in-memory database that requires 1 TB of RAM. Which EC2 instance family is most appropriate and cost-effective?

answers.A: C7i (compute-optimized): provides high CPU-to-memory ratio for compute-intensive workloads.
answers.B: R7i or X2idn (memory-optimized): purpose-built for high memory workloads; X-family instances provide up to 24 TB RAM.
answers.C: T4g (burstable general purpose): lowest cost, suitable for memory-intensive applications.
answers.D: G5 (GPU instances): GPU memory is separate from system RAM, providing high total memory.

explanation: R (memory-optimized) and X (high memory) instance families are designed for memory-intensive workloads. R instances provide up to 768 GB RAM, and X instances (X1, X2) provide up to 24 TB RAM — purpose-built for in-memory databases (SAP HANA, Redis, Memcached at scale). C-family (A) is compute-optimized with a lower memory-to-CPU ratio. T4g burstable (C) has limited RAM (up to 32 GB on t4g.2xlarge) and is designed for variable-load workloads, not consistently memory-heavy databases. GPU memory (D) is not accessible to in-memory databases.
tags: Selecting the appropriate instance family for a workload
Determining cost-effective AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate)

stem: A company runs an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with 2 reader instances for read scaling. During off-peak hours (10pm-6am), there is no read traffic. How can they reduce Aurora costs during off-peak hours?

answers.A: Delete the reader instances each evening and recreate them each morning.
answers.B: Use Aurora Auto Scaling: define a scaling policy based on average CPU or connections. Reader instances are automatically added or removed. During off-peak, the policy scales in to 0 reader instances.
answers.C: Switch to Aurora Serverless v2: compute scales to minimum capacity (0.5 ACUs) during idle periods.
answers.D: Stop the Aurora cluster nightly — Aurora supports cluster stopping for up to 7 days.

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales compute capacity continuously from 0.5 ACUs to the configured maximum, billing per ACU-second. During off-peak with no traffic, capacity scales to the minimum (0.5 ACUs = ~1 GB RAM), dramatically reducing cost compared to provisioned reader instances. Aurora Auto Scaling (B) can scale to 0 readers but has a scale-in cooldown and minimum replica count constraints — it may not scale to 0. Manual delete/create (A) risks prolonged provisioning time. Cluster stopping (D) stops the writer too, making the database unavailable.
tags: Database capacity planning (for example, capacity units)

stem: A company spends $50,000/month on RDS On-Demand instances that have been running consistently for 18 months with no signs of stopping. Which purchasing option would most reduce costs?

answers.A: Move all RDS instances to Spot — RDS supports Spot pricing for cost savings.
answers.B: Purchase 1-year Reserved Instances for the RDS instance types/sizes currently running — provides up to 42% discount vs On-Demand with All Upfront payment.
answers.C: Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances — provides up to 65% discount vs On-Demand.
answers.D: Switch to Aurora Serverless for all databases to eliminate reserved capacity costs.

explanation: RDS does not support Spot pricing (A is false). 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for RDS provide up to 65% discount versus On-Demand — on $50,000/month spend, this saves $32,500/month or $390,000/year. At 18 months of consistent usage, a 3-year commitment is justified. 1-year RIs (B) save up to 42% — significant but less than 3-year. Aurora Serverless (D) works for variable workloads but typically costs more than provisioned Aurora for high, consistent utilization workloads.
tags: AWS cost management service features (for example, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing)
AWS cost management tools with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Report)

stem: A company runs a legacy Java EE application on on-premises servers. The application cannot be modified and opens thousands of persistent database connections, causing frequent connection timeouts. The team is migrating the database to Amazon RDS MySQL. Which AWS service should they add to improve the reliability of the application without code changes?

answers.A: Enable Multi-AZ on the RDS instance to handle failover automatically.
answers.B: Place Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the RDS instance to pool and multiplex database connections.
answers.C: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache query results and reduce database load.
answers.D: Configure an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions in front of the application servers.

explanation: RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes connections, reducing the number of open connections to RDS. This requires no application code changes and directly solves connection exhaustion — a common legacy-app reliability issue. Multi-AZ addresses availability, not connection exhaustion.

stem: A machine learning team needs storage for training datasets that must be simultaneously accessible from 50 SageMaker training instances across multiple Availability Zones. The data is read-heavy, rarely written, and can reach 50 TB. Which storage solution provides the highest read throughput with the simplest multi-instance access pattern?

answers.A: Provision a single Amazon EBS io2 volume and attach it to a single EC2 instance that serves the data via NFS.
answers.B: Store the training data in Amazon S3 and configure SageMaker to use S3 as the input data source with File mode or Fast File mode.
answers.C: Use Amazon EFS in General Purpose mode, mount it on all training instances, and read data directly.
answers.D: Deploy an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system backed by S3 and mount it on every training instance.

explanation: S3 with SageMaker's native input modes (File or Fast File) is the standard pattern for multi-instance training at scale. EBS cannot be attached to multiple instances simultaneously for read/write. EFS works but is slower and more expensive for this read-heavy large-dataset pattern. FSx for Lustre is valid for HPC workloads but adds operational overhead.

Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)

stem: A company is choosing between Amazon EBS and Amazon EFS for a new workload. Their application runs on a single EC2 instance, requires sub-millisecond latency for random I/O, and processes a database with frequent read/write operations. Which storage service and configuration is most appropriate?

answers.A: Amazon EFS with Max I/O performance mode for high throughput.

stem: A media company streams video content globally. They want to run custom authentication logic and modify HTTP headers at the edge, as close to end users as possible, to reduce latency. The logic is stateless and executes in milliseconds. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.B: Run the authentication logic on EC2 instances in multiple Regions behind Route 53 latency-based routing.

It is purpose-built for stateless, low-latency logic at the CDN layer. A central Lambda origin would add round-trip latency. EC2 across regions adds management overhead. Wavelength is for ultra-low-latency 5G mobile use cases.

stem: A company processes IoT telemetry from factory floors around the world. The data must be analysed locally in near-real time before being sent to AWS. Network bandwidth to the cloud is limited. answers.A: Deploy AWS Lambda functions in multiple AWS Regions to process telemetry close to users.

answers.C: Use AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices at each factory to run local analytics and batch-sync data to S3.

explanation: AWS IoT Greengrass extends AWS compute to edge devices, enabling local Lambda execution and low-latency processing without constant cloud connectivity. Snowball Edge is for offline data transfer, not ongoing analytics. Lambda and Kinesis in a central Region don't solve the bandwidth or latency constraint.

stem: A company operates a hub-and-spoke network with a central shared-services VPC (hub) and 20 application VPCs (spokes). All spoke VPCs need to access on-premises resources through a single VPN connection in the hub VPC. Which AWS service enables this topology with the least operational overhead?

answers.A: AWS Transit Gateway, attaching all spoke VPCs and the VPN connection to a single transit gateway.
answers.B: VPC peering between every spoke VPC and the hub VPC, and enable route propagation through the hub.
answers.C: Configure VPN connections from each spoke VPC directly to the on-premises data centre.
answers.D: Deploy a third-party routing appliance on EC2 in the hub VPC to route between all spoke VPCs.

explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router, enabling transitive routing between attached VPCs and VPN/Direct Connect connections with a single managed resource. VPC peering is non-transitive (spoke-to-spoke traffic still can't flow), requiring N×(N-1)/2 peering connections. Separate VPNs per spoke is costly. A third-party appliance adds operational complexity.

stem: A SaaS company needs to give each customer tenant their own isolated VPC while allowing them to access a central shared-services VPC (containing databases and internal APIs) without exposing the shared VPC to the internet. Customer tenants must NOT be able to communicate with each other. Which topology satisfies these requirements?

answers.A: Peer all tenant VPCs to the shared-services VPC and enable transitive routing through the shared VPC.
answers.B: Use AWS PrivateLink to expose specific services from the shared-services VPC as VPC Endpoints, and create endpoint connections in each tenant VPC.
answers.C: Attach all VPCs to a Transit Gateway and use route tables to restrict communication between tenants.
answers.D: Deploy the shared services on EC2 instances with public IP addresses and restrict access using security groups.

explanation: AWS PrivateLink exposes specific services from the shared VPC as Interface Endpoints without any routing relationship between VPCs. Tenant VPCs cannot communicate with each other at all. VPC peering is non-transitive so tenants can't talk through the shared VPC, but it exposes the entire VPC CIDR. Transit Gateway route tables can isolate tenants but add operational overhead. Public IPs are a security anti-pattern.

stem: A financial services application requires the absolute lowest network latency between EC2 instances that process high-frequency trading data. The instances must exchange messages in microseconds. Which placement option achieves this?

answers.A: Place the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group within a single Availability Zone.
answers.B: Place the EC2 instances in a spread placement group across multiple Availability Zones.
answers.C: Deploy the EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones with an Application Load Balancer in front.
answers.D: Use AWS Local Zones to deploy the instances physically closer to the stock exchange.

explanation: Cluster placement groups pack instances physically close together on the same underlying hardware within a single AZ, providing the highest network throughput and lowest latency. Spread placement groups maximize fault tolerance by distributing instances across hardware — the opposite of what's needed here. Load balancers add latency. Local Zones address end-user latency, not inter-instance latency.

stem: A company runs a three-tier application and wants to maximize fault tolerance across hardware failures while accepting a small latency increase between tiers. Which EC2 placement strategy should they use?

answers.B: Partition placement group with all instances in a single partition.
answers.C: Spread placement group, distributing instances across distinct underlying hardware racks.
answers.D: No placement group; rely on default placement by AWS.

explanation: A spread placement group ensures each instance is placed on separate hardware with independent power and networking, reducing the blast radius of hardware failures. Cluster groups sacrifice fault isolation for low latency. Partition groups suit large distributed systems (HDFS, Cassandra). Default placement provides no guarantees about hardware isolation.
