answers.D: Deploy a NAT gateway in the VPC and configure on-premises routing to send all AWS public service traffic through the private VIF, through the VPC, and then out the NAT gateway to reach public endpoints.

explanation: A public VIF provides on-premises access to AWS public service endpoints (S3, SQS, etc.) by advertising AWS public IP ranges via BGP over Direct Connect, eliminating internet traversal. A private VIF connects to VPC private resources only and cannot natively reach public AWS endpoints. Option A is incorrect because a private VIF does not carry AWS public service prefixes; routing through NAT adds unnecessary complexity and latency. Option C (Site-to-Site VPN over private VIF) is a valid encryption pattern but does not solve the fundamental need to reach public endpoints without internet; split tunneling also does not help here. Option D uses NAT gateway to egress to the internet, which defeats the requirement to avoid the public internet. The correct solution is a dedicated public VIF.

stem: A healthcare company requires Layer 2 encryption for all data traversing its 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection to meet HIPAA compliance requirements. The company uses a transit VIF connected to an AWS Direct Connect Gateway and Transit Gateway to access 12 VPCs. The solution must not require changes to the existing BGP session or virtual interface configuration. Which solution meets these requirements?
tags: Implementing MACsec on Direct Connect connections for Layer 2 encryption

answers.A: Enable MACsec on the dedicated Direct Connect connection by associating a MACsec secret key (CKN/CAK pair) with the connection. MACsec encrypts traffic at Layer 2 on the physical link between the customer router and the AWS Direct Connect device, transparent to the existing virtual interfaces and BGP sessions.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the existing Direct Connect transit VIF to add IPsec encryption. Configure IKEv2 with AES-256 and configure BGP over the VPN tunnels to replace the existing Direct Connect BGP session.
answers.C: Enable TLS 1.3 encryption on all application endpoints within the 12 VPCs to encrypt data in transit at Layer 7, satisfying the HIPAA encryption requirement for data traversing Direct Connect.
answers.D: Configure an AWS Network Firewall in each of the 12 VPCs in TLS inspection mode to encrypt outbound traffic before it traverses the Direct Connect connection to the on-premises network.

explanation: MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) provides Layer 2 encryption on the physical Direct Connect link between the customer device and AWS. It is configured directly on the dedicated connection (not on virtual interfaces) and is transparent to BGP sessions and virtual interfaces. This means no changes to existing VIF or BGP configuration are needed. Option B (IPsec VPN over Direct Connect) operates at Layer 3/4 and requires reconfiguring BGP, which violates the requirement. Option C (TLS) is application-layer (Layer 7) encryption and does not satisfy a Layer 2 encryption requirement; compliance auditors may require link-level encryption. Option D (Network Firewall) provides inspection and filtering, not Layer 2 link encryption, and is architecturally incorrect for this use case.

stem: A network operations team manages VPC infrastructure across 40 AWS accounts. They must implement a solution to automatically remediate any security group rule that allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 within 5 minutes of creation. The solution must work across all accounts with minimal per-account configuration. Which approach meets these requirements?
tags: AWS Config rules for network compliance monitoring
Automating network compliance checks using AWS Config custom rules
AWS Lambda for network automation tasks

answers.A: Deploy an AWS CloudTrail trail in each account and create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that triggers an SNS notification when a security group rule allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. Have the security team manually remediate violations within the required window.
answers.B: Use AWS Security Hub with the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark standard enabled in each account. Configure Security Hub to generate findings for overly permissive security groups and integrate with a ticketing system for remediation tracking.
answers.C: Deploy an AWS Config rule using the managed rule restricted-ssh in each account. Configure the Config rule with an SNS notification to alert the network team, who will then use Systems Manager Run Command to revoke the rule.
answers.D: Deploy an AWS Config conformance pack using AWS Organizations that includes the restricted-ssh managed rule with an automatic SSM remediation action. The remediation action invokes an SSM Automation document to revoke the offending security group ingress rule across all accounts.

explanation: AWS Config conformance packs deployed via AWS Organizations provide centralized, automated compliance enforcement across all member accounts with minimal per-account configuration. Pairing the restricted-ssh Config rule with an SSM Automation remediation action enables automatic revocation of offending rules, meeting the 5-minute remediation SLA without human intervention. Option A (CloudTrail + SNS + manual remediation) requires human action and cannot guarantee the 5-minute window. Option B (Security Hub) generates findings and supports ticketing but does not natively auto-remediate within the required timeframe. Option C deploys Config rules but relies on manual remediation by the network team, which is not automated and may not meet the 5-minute SLA. Option D is the only fully automated, organization-wide approach.

stem: A company operates 60 AWS accounts and requires a centralized solution to ensure that all VPCs enforce a consistent set of AWS WAF rules protecting their internet-facing Application Load Balancers. The security team must be able to update WAF rules centrally and have them propagate automatically. New accounts joining the AWS Organization must receive the WAF policy automatically. Which solution meets these requirements?
tags: AWS Firewall Manager for centralized firewall policy management
AWS Firewall Manager for centralized network security policy
Implementing AWS Firewall Manager to deploy consistent WAF and Network Firewall policies

answers.A: Create an AWS Config rule that detects ALBs without WAF associations. Configure a Lambda remediation function that attaches a pre-defined WAF web ACL to non-compliant ALBs. Deploy this Config rule and Lambda to each account using AWS CloudFormation StackSets.
answers.B: In the AWS Firewall Manager administrator account, create a WAF policy scoped to the AWS Organization. Define the required managed rule groups and custom rules. Enable automatic remediation so Firewall Manager deploys and enforces the web ACL across all existing and new accounts.
answers.C: Use AWS Security Hub to create custom actions that trigger a Lambda function when an ALB finding is generated. The Lambda function attaches the standard WAF web ACL to the identified ALB in the affected account using cross-account IAM roles.
answers.D: Deploy a centralized WAF web ACL in a shared services account. Use Amazon API Gateway as a reverse proxy in each member account so all ALB traffic routes through the shared account where the WAF is applied before reaching the actual ALBs.

explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is purpose-built for centralized security policy enforcement across an AWS Organization. A WAF policy in Firewall Manager automatically deploys and enforces the defined WAF web ACL to all in-scope resources (internet-facing ALBs) across existing and new accounts as they join the organization. Policy updates propagate automatically. Option A (Config + Lambda + StackSets) can detect and remediate but requires manual StackSet management and has higher operational overhead. Option C (Security Hub + Lambda) is reactive and event-driven but does not provide proactive, preventive enforcement or automatic propagation to new accounts. Option D (API Gateway proxy + shared WAF) is architecturally complex, introduces a single point of failure, and significantly increases latency.

stem: A company is deploying AWS Client VPN to provide remote access for 500 engineers to private VPC resources. The security team mandates certificate-based mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication and requires that client certificates be issued from the company's own internal PKI hierarchy (not a public CA). The solution must enable easy certificate lifecycle management including automated rotation. Which combination of services should the network engineer use?
tags: AWS Private Certificate Authority (AWS Private CA)
Client VPN with certificate-based and Active Directory authentication
Configuring AWS Client VPN with mutual certificate authentication or Active Directory integration
Deploying AWS Private CA to issue private certificates for internal services

answers.A: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue public TLS certificates for the Client VPN server endpoint. Generate self-signed client certificates using OpenSSL and distribute them manually to engineers. Import both into ACM for use with Client VPN.
answers.B: Deploy a third-party CA appliance on an EC2 instance in a private subnet. Issue server and client certificates from this CA. Configure Client VPN to trust the self-managed EC2 CA and use Lambda to trigger certificate renewals via a scheduled EventBridge rule.
answers.C: Create an AWS Private CA (subordinate CA) under the company's internal root CA hierarchy. Use Private CA to issue the Client VPN server certificate and client certificates. Store client certificate private keys in Secrets Manager. Configure Client VPN mutual authentication to trust the Private CA. Use ACM Private CA managed renewal for automated rotation.
answers.D: Configure Client VPN with Active Directory authentication using AWS Directory Service. Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to issue server-side public certificates. Disable client certificate authentication since AD provides identity verification, and rely on IAM for additional authorization.

explanation: AWS Private CA (formerly ACM PCA) allows organizations to create a private CA hierarchy that integrates with their existing root CA. It issues private certificates for Client VPN server and client authentication, supports automated managed renewal, and integrates with Secrets Manager for secure credential storage. This meets the mTLS requirement with company-controlled PKI. Option A uses public ACM certificates (not suitable for a private internal PKI) and manually distributed self-signed client certs, which lack lifecycle management. Option B (EC2 CA) works but is operationally burdensome compared to the managed AWS Private CA service. Option D removes mTLS client certificate authentication in favor of AD-only auth, which does not meet the stated mTLS requirement.

stem: A security engineer suspects that compromised EC2 instances in a VPC are exfiltrating data. VPC Flow Logs are enabled, but they only show IP addresses, ports, and byte counts, not packet payload content. The engineer must capture the full packet content from specific suspicious EC2 instances for forensic analysis without installing agents on the instances. Which solution meets these requirements?
tags: VPC traffic mirroring for packet-level analysis
Using traffic mirroring to capture and analyze packets for troubleshooting

answers.A: Enable VPC Traffic Mirroring on the ENIs of the suspicious EC2 instances. Configure a traffic mirror target (an NLB or ENI of a monitoring appliance) and a traffic mirror filter to capture the relevant flows. Direct mirrored packets to a packet capture tool on the monitoring instance for deep packet inspection.
answers.B: Enable VPC Flow Logs with the version 5 format to capture additional metadata fields including TCP flags and packet-level details. Export the enhanced flow logs to Amazon S3 and analyze them using Amazon Athena to reconstruct session payloads.
answers.C: Use Amazon GuardDuty with VPC Flow Log analysis enabled. GuardDuty performs anomaly detection and behavioral analysis on the flow records and will automatically capture suspicious payloads from flagged EC2 instances for forensic review.
answers.D: Deploy an AWS Network Firewall in the VPC with stateful deep packet inspection rules. Configure the firewall to log all traffic in PCAP format to an S3 bucket, then filter the logs to isolate traffic from the suspicious EC2 instances.

explanation: VPC Traffic Mirroring copies network traffic from the ENI of a monitored instance and sends it to a target (NLB or a monitoring appliance ENI) without requiring agents on the source instances. This allows full packet capture for forensic analysis, including payload content. Option B (VPC Flow Logs v5) does not capture payload data; flow logs are metadata only regardless of version. Option C (GuardDuty) provides threat detection based on flow log analysis but does not capture raw packet payloads for forensic examination. Option D (Network Firewall) can log packet headers and match patterns via stateful rules but does not produce PCAP-format captures of arbitrary traffic flows from specific instances.

stem: A multinational company operates AWS infrastructure across 6 Regions and 120 accounts. They need a solution to build a global private network with distinct network segments for production, development, and shared services, applying different routing and security policies per segment. The solution must support centralized routing policy management and allow cross-segment traffic only for explicitly permitted flows. Which service best meets these requirements?
tags: AWS Cloud WAN for global network management

answers.A: Deploy a Transit Gateway in each Region with separate route tables per segment (production, development, shared services). Establish Transit Gateway inter-Region peering between all 6 Regions and manually configure static routes to control cross-segment traffic.
answers.B: Use AWS PrivateLink to connect services across accounts and Regions. Create endpoint services in the shared services account and interface endpoints in production and development accounts to enforce explicit access control per connection.
answers.C: Implement a hub-and-spoke topology using a shared Transit Gateway in each Region with VPC attachments. Use Transit Gateway route table blackhole routes to block cross-segment traffic and share Transit Gateways across accounts using AWS RAM.
answers.D: Deploy AWS Cloud WAN with a global network policy that defines separate segments for production, development, and shared services. Attach VPCs from all Regions and accounts to the Cloud WAN core network. Use segment actions and attachment policies to permit only explicitly allowed cross-segment traffic flows.

explanation: AWS Cloud WAN is purpose-built for global, multi-Region, multi-account network management with a centralized policy. Segments in Cloud WAN provide isolated routing domains (similar to VRFs), and cross-segment connectivity is controlled through segment actions in the global network policy. This eliminates the need to manually manage inter-Region Transit Gateway peering and per-Region route tables. Option A (per-Region TGW with peering) works but requires extensive manual configuration across 6 Regions and lacks centralized policy management. Option B (PrivateLink) is for service-level access, not network-wide routing segmentation. Option C (shared TGW per Region) provides segmentation within a Region but still requires manual peering and inter-Region coordination, lacking the centralized global policy of Cloud WAN.

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with 80 member accounts. The network security team must enforce a policy that prevents any member account from modifying or deleting VPC Flow Log configurations once they are created. The policy must also prevent disabling of AWS CloudTrail in any account. Which is the most effective mechanism to enforce these constraints?
tags: Service Control Policies (SCPs) for network governance
AWS CloudTrail for network API activity auditing

answers.A: Create Service Control Policies (SCPs) that deny the ec2:DeleteFlowLogs, ec2:StopFlowLogs, cloudtrail:StopLogging, and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail actions. Attach these SCPs to the root of the AWS Organization so they apply to all member accounts and cannot be overridden by member account administrators.
answers.B: Deploy an AWS Config rule in each account that checks for VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail status. Configure automatic remediation using SSM Automation to re-enable them if disabled. Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy this configuration across all accounts.
answers.C: Enable AWS Security Hub in all accounts with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard. Configure Security Hub to generate critical findings and send PagerDuty alerts when Flow Logs or CloudTrail are disabled, enabling rapid human remediation.
answers.D: Create IAM permission boundaries in each member account that deny the flow log and CloudTrail deletion actions. Apply these permission boundaries to all IAM roles and users using a CloudFormation StackSet, and use AWS IAM Identity Center to enforce boundary assignment.

explanation: SCPs are the correct mechanism to preventively deny specific API actions across all accounts in an AWS Organization. Unlike reactive controls, SCPs apply regardless of IAM permissions in member accounts. Even an account root user cannot perform SCP-denied actions. Denying ec2:DeleteFlowLogs, ec2:StopFlowLogs, cloudtrail:StopLogging, and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail at the Organizational root level provides the strongest guardrail. Option B (Config + SSM remediation) is reactive, not preventive; there is a window between a deletion and remediation. Option C (Security Hub) is detection-only and requires human response. Option D (IAM permission boundaries) are applied to identities within an account but do not prevent an account administrator from creating new roles without the boundary or using the account root.

stem: A data analytics company runs large-scale ETL jobs on EC2 instances in a private subnet that read large datasets from Amazon S3. The company currently uses a NAT gateway for all egress traffic, incurring significant data transfer charges. The engineering team wants to eliminate S3 data transfer costs through the NAT gateway while maintaining private connectivity. The solution must require minimal configuration changes. Which solution best meets these requirements?
tags: VPC endpoint cost optimization versus NAT gateway costs
Replacing NAT Gateway usage with VPC endpoints where applicable to reduce costs

answers.A: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the private subnet. Update the EC2 instance security groups to allow HTTPS traffic to the S3 endpoint ENI, and configure a bucket policy that restricts access to traffic originating from the interface endpoint.
answers.B: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Add an entry to the route table of the private subnet pointing the S3 prefix list to the gateway endpoint. Traffic to S3 will route through the endpoint without traversing the NAT gateway, and there are no data processing charges for gateway endpoints.
answers.C: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket and update application code to use the Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Transfer Acceleration routes traffic over the AWS global network, bypassing the NAT gateway and reducing costs.
answers.D: Move the EC2 instances to a public subnet and assign Elastic IP addresses. Direct S3 traffic over the internet gateway, which has no per-GB data processing charges, while keeping the NAT gateway for other private subnet resources.

explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 is free (no data processing charges) and routes S3 traffic within the AWS network without traversing the NAT gateway, eliminating NAT gateway data processing costs. Adding the S3 prefix list route to the private subnet route table is the only required configuration change. Option A (interface endpoint) also works but incurs hourly charges per endpoint ENI and per-GB data processing fees, making it more expensive than a gateway endpoint for high-volume S3 access. Option C (Transfer Acceleration) is for optimizing upload/download speeds for geographically distant users; it does not eliminate NAT gateway costs. Option D (moving to public subnet) eliminates the NAT gateway but introduces security risks by exposing instances directly to the internet.

stem: A platform engineering team manages 200 VPCs across 30 accounts. They need to automate IP address allocation so that when a new VPC creation event occurs, the VPC automatically receives a non-overlapping CIDR from a centrally managed pool. The solution must prevent duplicate CIDR assignments and provide visibility into allocated and available ranges across all accounts. Which solution meets these requirements?
tags: VPC IPAM (IP Address Manager) for automated IP management
Implementing VPC IPAM for centralized IP address management across accounts

answers.A: Maintain an IP address inventory spreadsheet updated manually by the networking team. Implement an approval workflow in AWS Service Catalog so that new VPC requests require network team sign-off before CIDR ranges are assigned from the spreadsheet.
answers.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that queries a DynamoDB table of allocated CIDRs, calculates the next available range, and returns it when invoked. Trigger the function via a CloudWatch Events rule that fires on VPC creation API calls captured by CloudTrail.
answers.C: Deploy Amazon VPC IPAM with a pool hierarchy that spans the AWS Organization. Create Regional pools with defined CIDR allocations. Configure VPCs to allocate CIDRs from IPAM pools at creation time. IPAM enforces non-overlap and tracks usage across all accounts and Regions.
answers.D: Use AWS Config with a custom rule that checks VPC CIDRs for overlaps against a reference CIDR list stored in an S3 bucket. Configure automatic remediation to delete conflicting VPCs detected after creation.

explanation: Amazon VPC IPAM is purpose-built for centralized IP address management across an AWS Organization. It maintains hierarchical IP pools, enforces non-overlapping CIDR allocations, and provides a unified view of all allocated and available ranges. VPCs can be provisioned to draw CIDRs directly from IPAM pools, ensuring automation without manual intervention. Option A (spreadsheet) is manual and error-prone. Option B (Lambda + DynamoDB) can work but is a custom solution with potential race conditions if multiple VPCs are created simultaneously, and it lacks the native organization-wide visibility that IPAM provides. Option D (Config rule) is reactive — it detects overlaps after creation and deleting a VPC after creation is disruptive and not a preventive control.

stem: A network operations team wants to monitor a newly deployed Transit Gateway connecting 20 VPCs and two Direct Connect attachments. They need real-time visibility into bytes transferred per attachment, automated alerting when any attachment throughput drops to zero (indicating a routing failure), and a historical dashboard showing 30 days of trends. Which approach fulfills all three requirements most efficiently?
tags: CloudWatch metrics for networking services (Direct Connect, VPN, NAT Gateway, etc.)
Configuring CloudWatch alarms for network performance thresholds

answers.A: Enable VPC Flow Logs on all 20 VPCs and aggregate them in a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query flow records and build Grafana dashboards. Create an EventBridge scheduled rule that runs an Athena query hourly and sends SNS alerts when byte counts are zero.
answers.B: Register the Transit Gateway with AWS Network Manager. Enable Transit Gateway metrics in CloudWatch (BytesIn, BytesOut per attachment). Create CloudWatch alarms on BytesOut for each attachment with threshold 0 to trigger SNS notifications. Build a CloudWatch dashboard with 30-day retention widgets for historical trends.
answers.C: Deploy a network monitoring EC2 instance in each VPC with packet capture agents. Aggregate SNMP traps to a central collector. Configure alerts in the third-party monitoring tool when interface counters drop to zero, and use the tool's built-in dashboarding for 30-day trends.
answers.D: Enable AWS CloudTrail in all accounts and create Athena queries over CloudTrail management events to detect changes in Transit Gateway attachment states. Set up CloudWatch Logs metric filters on CloudTrail to detect DetachVpc or DeleteTGWAttachment API calls as a proxy for connectivity failures.

explanation: Transit Gateway publishes per-attachment CloudWatch metrics (BytesIn, BytesOut, PacketsDropped) natively. CloudWatch alarms can trigger SNS notifications when BytesOut drops to zero, satisfying the real-time alert requirement. CloudWatch dashboards with appropriate time ranges provide 30-day historical views. AWS Network Manager enhances this with topology visualization and centralized monitoring. Option A (VPC Flow Logs + Athena) captures packet-level data but Athena queries are not real-time; the hourly schedule does not meet real-time alerting. Option C (EC2 agents + SNMP) introduces operational overhead and is not native to the Transit Gateway monitoring stack. Option D (CloudTrail API events) detects configuration changes, not throughput drops; a routing failure may not generate any API call.

stem: A company is deploying a PCI DSS-compliant workload on AWS. The architecture requires all inbound internet traffic to be inspected by a stateful IDS/IPS before reaching application servers, and all outbound traffic from application servers must also be inspected before leaving the VPC. The company uses EC2-based application servers in private subnets and an internet gateway. Which architecture satisfies PCI DSS inspection requirements with the least operational overhead?
tags: AWS Network Firewall and its stateful and stateless rule groups
Deploying AWS Network Firewall in centralized or distributed architectures

answers.A: Deploy AWS WAF on an ALB in a public subnet for inbound inspection. Place application servers in private subnets behind the ALB. Configure a NAT gateway for outbound traffic. Use security groups to restrict unauthorized cross-tier access.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in a dedicated firewall subnet. Configure the internet gateway route table to send inbound traffic through Network Firewall endpoints. Configure application subnet route tables to route outbound traffic through the firewall before reaching the NAT gateway.
answers.C: Place EC2 application servers in public subnets and assign Elastic IPs. Attach AWS WAF to the internet gateway to inspect all HTTP and HTTPS traffic. Use network ACLs to restrict non-HTTP protocols at the subnet boundary.
answers.D: Enable AWS Shield Advanced with proactive engagement on the internet gateway. Configure DDoS-specific protections and use restrictive security group rules on application server ENIs to block unauthorized inbound and outbound connections.

explanation: AWS Network Firewall is a managed stateful IDS/IPS that can inspect both inbound and outbound traffic. Deploying it in a dedicated firewall subnet with symmetric routing (all inbound internet traffic routes through the firewall endpoint before reaching application subnets, and all outbound traffic from application subnets routes through the firewall endpoint) provides full bidirectional inspection required by PCI DSS. Option A (WAF on ALB) covers inbound HTTP/HTTPS but does not inspect outbound traffic from application servers or non-HTTP protocols. Option C (WAF on internet gateway) is incorrect; WAF cannot be directly attached to an internet gateway and only inspects Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic. Option D (Shield Advanced) provides DDoS mitigation, not stateful IDS/IPS inspection of all traffic flows.

stem: A company runs a shared microservices platform that other business units access from their own VPCs. The platform VPC contains a service running on an NLB on port 8443. Business units have VPCs in the same Region (some in the same account, some in different accounts) and must access the service without VPC peering or Transit Gateway to keep blast radius small. New business units are frequently onboarded. Which solution allows secure, scalable access to the service?
tags: AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints and endpoint services
Designing AWS PrivateLink endpoint services to share applications across VPCs and accounts
Deploying centralized VPC interface endpoints shared across multiple VPCs

answers.A: Create a VPC endpoint service in the platform account backed by the NLB. Grant the business unit accounts permission to create endpoints to the service. In each business unit VPC, create an interface VPC endpoint pointing to the endpoint service. Business units access the service using the endpoint's private DNS name.
answers.B: Peer the platform VPC with each business unit VPC using VPC peering. Update route tables on both sides of each peering connection to allow traffic to the NLB subnet CIDR. Add NLB security group rules permitting traffic from each business unit VPC CIDR.
answers.C: Deploy a Transit Gateway and attach the platform VPC and all business unit VPCs. Create a shared route table that propagates routes from all attachments. Business units route traffic to the NLB using Transit Gateway. Restrict cross-VPC access using security groups.
answers.D: Assign an Elastic IP to the NLB in the platform VPC. Business units access the service over the internet using the EIP and enforce access control using the NLB's security groups to allowlist business unit NAT gateway IPs.

explanation: AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint services) is the purpose-built mechanism to share services across VPCs and accounts without VPC peering or Transit Gateway. It keeps network connectivity scoped to the specific service port, minimizing blast radius. The endpoint service owner controls which accounts can create endpoints, supporting frequent onboarding. Option B (VPC peering) allows full VPC-to-VPC routing rather than service-specific access, increasing blast radius; it also does not scale well to many VPCs. Option C (Transit Gateway) routes all traffic between all attached VPCs, significantly increasing blast radius and requiring route table management for every new attachment. Option D (Elastic IP over internet) routes traffic over the public internet, reducing security and not meeting private connectivity requirements.

stem: A high-frequency trading company runs latency-sensitive algorithms on a cluster of EC2 c5n.18xlarge instances in us-east-1. Inter-instance communication must achieve the lowest possible latency with the highest throughput and the minimum number of network hops. The cluster runs in a single Availability Zone. Which configuration achieves these goals?
tags: Enhanced Networking (SR-IOV) and Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)
Network bandwidth limits for EC2 instance types

answers.A: Deploy the instances in a spread placement group across multiple Availability Zones to maximize fault tolerance. Enable ENA on each instance for enhanced networking and use jumbo frames (MTU 9001) for large data transfers between instances.
answers.B: Launch the instances in a partition placement group within a single AZ. Configure ENA Enhanced Networking and use an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for RDMA-based MPI communication. Use jumbo frames for bulk data transfer.
answers.C: Place instances in a dedicated host in a single AZ. Enable ENA Enhanced Networking and configure a 25 Gbps Enhanced Networking adapter. Use security groups to minimize filtering overhead on the data path between instances.
answers.D: Launch all instances in a cluster placement group within a single AZ. Enable Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) on each instance for low-latency, high-throughput OS-bypass networking. Configure jumbo frames (MTU 9001) to maximize throughput for large message transfers.

explanation: Cluster placement groups place instances physically close together within a single AZ to minimize network latency and maximize throughput between instances. Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) provides OS-bypass networking (similar to RDMA), enabling extremely low latency for HPC and financial workloads. c5n instances support EFA. Jumbo frames (MTU 9001) reduce header overhead for large transfers. This combination is the AWS-recommended approach for latency-sensitive clustered workloads. Option A (spread placement group) distributes instances for fault tolerance, which increases inter-instance distance and latency, the opposite of what is needed. Option B (partition placement group) is designed for distributed workloads requiring fault isolation between partitions, not minimum latency between all nodes. Option C (dedicated host) provides hardware isolation for licensing or compliance but does not optimize networking performance to the degree of cluster placement groups and EFA.

stem: A company has 10 application VPCs and a centralized DNS VPC with Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints. An on-premises DNS server forwards queries for .corp.example.com to the Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. The company now needs application VPCs in other AWS accounts to also be able to resolve the same .corp.example.com private hosted zones and on-premises names without deploying separate Resolver endpoints in each account. What is the most operationally efficient architecture?
tags: Sharing Resolver rules across accounts using AWS RAM
Implementing centralized DNS architectures using shared services VPCs
Route 53 Resolver endpoint deployment in VPCs

answers.A: In each application VPC account, deploy separate Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints. Create identical forwarding rules for the on-premises domain. Associate the private hosted zones with each application VPC. This provides independent DNS resolution per account.
answers.B: In the centralized DNS VPC account, create Route 53 Resolver forwarding rules for on-premises domains and share them with all application VPC accounts using AWS RAM. Associate the private hosted zones with the application VPCs. Application VPC DNS queries use the shared rules to reach the centralized Resolver outbound endpoints.
answers.C: Configure VPC peering between the centralized DNS VPC and each application VPC. Update DNS settings on the application VPCs to use the centralized DNS VPC's Route 53 Resolver endpoint IP addresses as custom DNS servers, bypassing AWS-provided DNS entirely.
answers.D: Create a Transit Gateway and attach all VPCs. Configure the Transit Gateway route table to forward DNS UDP/53 traffic from application VPCs to the centralized DNS VPC. Enable multicast on the Transit Gateway to broadcast DNS responses back to requesting VPCs.

explanation: Sharing Route 53 Resolver forwarding rules via AWS RAM allows all application VPC accounts to use the centralized Resolver outbound endpoints without deploying endpoints in each account. Application VPCs send DNS queries to the VPC resolver (169.254.169.253), which evaluates shared forwarding rules and routes on-premises domain queries through the centralized outbound endpoints. Private hosted zone associations ensure AWS-native resolution works across accounts. Option A (per-account endpoints) works but requires deploying and managing Resolver endpoints in every account, which is operationally expensive. Option C (VPC peering + custom DNS servers) bypasses AWS-provided DNS and creates a non-standard, fragile architecture; application VPCs would need route table entries to reach the DNS VPC endpoint IPs. Option D misuses Transit Gateway multicast for DNS, which is not a supported or practical pattern.

stem: A company's security team wants to detect when EC2 instances in a VPC communicate with known command-and-control (C2) IP addresses or when instances begin performing unusual network port scans. The solution must work without installing agents on EC2 instances and must generate actionable findings that integrate with the company's SIEM. Which solution meets these requirements?
tags: Amazon GuardDuty threat detection and VPC Flow Log analysis
Enabling and configuring GuardDuty for network threat detection across accounts

answers.A: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts and Regions. GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS query logs, and CloudTrail events without requiring agents. It uses threat intelligence feeds to detect C2 communications and behavioral analytics to identify port scanning. Export findings to Amazon EventBridge and forward to the SIEM via a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
answers.B: Enable VPC Flow Logs in all VPCs and export them to Amazon S3. Build Athena queries to scan for known C2 IP addresses from a manually maintained threat intelligence list. Schedule Athena queries to run hourly and publish results to SNS, which forwards alerts to the SIEM.
answers.C: Deploy AWS Network Firewall with stateful rules that block traffic to known malicious IPs using AWS-managed threat intelligence rule groups. Configure the firewall alert logs to stream to Kinesis Data Firehose and forward to the SIEM for analysis.
answers.D: Enable Amazon Inspector on all EC2 instances to perform continuous network reachability assessments. Inspector identifies exposure of instance ports to the internet and network paths that could be exploited, generating SIEM-compatible findings.

explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is purpose-built for agentless threat detection using VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events. It maintains continuously updated threat intelligence feeds to detect C2 communications and uses machine learning to detect port scanning behaviors. Findings are native to EventBridge for SIEM integration. Option B (manual Athena queries + manually maintained threat intel list) requires significant operational effort and the hourly schedule creates detection gaps. Option C (Network Firewall) actively blocks known threats but does not provide behavioral analytics for port scanning detection and only integrates at the enforcement layer, not detection-and-investigation. Option D (Amazon Inspector) assesses network exposure and vulnerabilities, not real-time behavioral anomalies like C2 communications or port scans.

stem: A company is building a multi-tier e-commerce application. The architecture requires an Application Load Balancer to terminate HTTPS and route to backend microservices, while also needing to forward the original client certificate information to backends for mTLS-based client authentication at the application layer. The backend services need the client certificate subject and issuer to make authorization decisions. Which ALB configuration meets these requirements?
tags: Implementing mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication on load balancers
Application Load Balancer (ALB) features including content-based routing, host-based routing, and path-based routing

answers.A: Configure the ALB listener with an HTTPS security policy that enforces TLS 1.2 minimum. Enable ALB access logs to capture client IP and TLS session details. Deploy a Lambda@Edge function on CloudFront in front of the ALB to extract client certificate metadata and append it as HTTP headers before forwarding to the ALB.
answers.B: Configure the ALB HTTPS listener with mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication mode set to passthrough or verify. When set to verify, the ALB validates the client certificate against a trust store and forwards the certificate metadata (subject, issuer, serial number) as X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-* HTTP headers to the backend target groups.
answers.C: Terminate TLS at the ALB without mTLS. Configure a custom header X-Client-Cert on the ALB listener rule that is set to a static value identifying the client. Backend services read this header to determine the client identity for authorization decisions.
answers.D: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer configured for TLS passthrough. The NLB passes encrypted traffic directly to backend EC2 instances where TLS termination and client certificate validation occurs at the application layer. Use a target group with TLS protocol.

explanation: ALB supports mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication on HTTPS listeners. In verify mode, the ALB validates the client certificate against a configured trust store (AWS Certificate Manager or custom CA) and forwards certificate attributes (subject, issuer, serial number, SANs) as HTTP headers (X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-*) to backends. This allows backends to make authorization decisions without re-implementing TLS termination. Option A (Lambda@Edge) is for CloudFront distributions, not ALB; it cannot intercept client certificates directly at the ALB layer. Option C (static custom header) does not provide real certificate metadata; the backend has no way to verify the header value is authentic. Option D (NLB TLS passthrough) does support end-to-end encryption but requires the backend applications to handle TLS termination and mTLS, increasing application complexity and not leveraging the ALB built-in mTLS capability.

stem: A company uses AWS Site-to-Site VPN with two tunnels to provide connectivity from its on-premises data center to a VPC. Both tunnels terminate on the same Virtual Private Gateway. The operations team notices that all traffic consistently flows through Tunnel 1, leaving Tunnel 2 idle. The on-premises router supports ECMP. The team wants both tunnels to carry traffic simultaneously for load distribution. What change will achieve active/active ECMP across both tunnels?
tags: Site-to-Site VPN tunnel configuration, IKE versions, and encryption parameters
Route priority and BGP path selection with Direct Connect and VPN

answers.A: Enable VPN acceleration on the Site-to-Site VPN connection using AWS Global Accelerator. Accelerated VPN uses anycast and automatically distributes traffic across both tunnels based on network conditions.
answers.B: Modify the VPN connection to use static routing instead of BGP. Add two identical static routes to the VGW, one per tunnel. This forces the VGW to balance traffic across both tunnels using its built-in load balancing.
answers.C: Increase the tunnel MTU on Tunnel 2 to be larger than Tunnel 1. The on-premises router will prefer the higher MTU path for larger packets, causing some traffic to shift to Tunnel 2, creating natural load distribution.
answers.D: Migrate the Site-to-Site VPN to use Transit Gateway instead of a Virtual Private Gateway. Transit Gateway supports ECMP for VPN and can distribute traffic across both BGP-enabled tunnels simultaneously when equal-cost routes are advertised, enabling active/active load sharing.

explanation: Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)-attached Site-to-Site VPN does not support ECMP; it uses only one tunnel at a time for a given flow, with the second tunnel as standby. Transit Gateway, by contrast, natively supports ECMP across multiple VPN tunnels when BGP is used and equal-cost routes are received. Migrating to TGW attachment allows both tunnels to carry traffic simultaneously when the on-premises router uses ECMP. Option A (Accelerated VPN) improves performance via Global Accelerator anycast but does not enable ECMP load sharing across both tunnels. Option B (static routing on VGW) does not enable ECMP; VGW is not designed for multi-tunnel load balancing. Option C (MTU difference) does not distribute traffic by design and creates unpredictable behavior rather than proper ECMP load sharing.

stem: A company is implementing a network landing zone for a new AWS Organization. The network team wants to ensure that all new accounts automatically receive a baseline network configuration: a VPC with predefined CIDR ranges, standard subnets, VPC Flow Logs enabled, and a Transit Gateway attachment to the hub VPC. The configuration must be applied within minutes of account creation with no manual steps. Which approach best automates this?
tags: AWS Control Tower and Landing Zone for network guardrails
AWS Lambda for network automation tasks
Implementing Control Tower customizations for network baseline configurations

answers.A: Require account requestors to submit a request through an internal portal. The network team reviews the request, manually provisions the VPC using the AWS console, enables Flow Logs, and requests a Transit Gateway attachment approval. Target SLA is 1 business day.
answers.B: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets targeting all accounts in the Organization. When a new account is added, manually trigger the StackSet to deploy the baseline VPC template. Monitor StackSet operation status in the CloudFormation console.
answers.C: Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory to provision new accounts. Customize the baseline using Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) or Control Tower customizations. Define a CloudFormation template or Terraform module that deploys the VPC, subnets, Flow Logs, and Transit Gateway attachment. Control Tower triggers the customization automatically on account vending.
answers.D: Configure an EventBridge rule in the management account that triggers on the CreateAccount API event. The rule invokes a Lambda function that assumes a role in the new account and runs AWS CLI commands to create the VPC, subnets, enable Flow Logs, and attach the Transit Gateway.

explanation: AWS Control Tower Account Factory (with customizations via AFT or native customizations) is the purpose-built mechanism for automatic baseline configuration of new AWS accounts. When a new account is vended through Account Factory, the defined customizations (CloudFormation templates or Terraform modules) are applied automatically, delivering VPC configuration, Flow Logs, and Transit Gateway attachments within minutes. Option A (manual process) cannot meet the no-manual-steps requirement. Option B (manually triggering StackSets) requires human action and does not fully automate the process. Option D (EventBridge + Lambda) is a valid custom automation approach but is significantly more complex to build, test, and maintain compared to the managed Control Tower customization framework, and handling the newly created account IAM role assumption timing reliably requires additional coordination.

stem: A financial services company runs a multi-tier application where an Application Load Balancer (ALB) terminates TLS from clients, and the backend EC2 instances communicate with an Amazon RDS database. The security team mandates mutual TLS (mTLS) between the ALB and the backend instances. The company uses AWS Certificate Manager Private CA (ACM Private CA) to issue certificates internally. Which approach correctly implements mTLS between the ALB and the backend EC2 instances while minimizing operational overhead?
tags: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM and Private CA)

answers.A: Configure the ALB listener with a self-signed certificate pinned to each backend instance certificate. Deploy a mutual TLS listener policy using a manually distributed CA bundle and rotate certificates quarterly.
answers.B: Enable end-to-end encryption by placing a Network Load Balancer in front of the ALB, configure TCP passthrough on the NLB, and terminate mTLS at the EC2 instances using OpenSSL with certificates issued by the on-premises PKI.
answers.C: Issue server certificates to EC2 instances from ACM Private CA, configure the ALB HTTPS listener with a mutual authentication trust store referencing the Private CA certificate, and use AWS Systems Manager to automate certificate renewal on the instances.
answers.D: Use ACM to issue public certificates for both the ALB and the backend instances, configure the ALB target group with HTTPS protocol, and rely on the ALB health checks to validate backend certificate validity.

explanation: C is correct because ALB supports mutual TLS authentication through a trust store that references a CA certificate. Using ACM Private CA to issue certificates for backend instances and configuring the ALB mTLS trust store with the Private CA root certificate implements the requirement. AWS Systems Manager automation reduces the operational overhead of certificate renewal on instances. A is wrong because ALBs do not support certificate pinning in listener policies and self-signed certificates distributed manually are not a scalable or supported solution. B is wrong because placing an NLB for TCP passthrough bypasses the ALB mTLS requirement at the ALB layer and adds unnecessary complexity. D is wrong because ACM public certificates can only be installed on ALBs and CloudFront endpoints, not on EC2 instances directly; mutual authentication requires a trust store configuration on the ALB.

stem: A company uses AWS Direct Connect for its hybrid connectivity between an on-premises data center and AWS. The security team has determined that a threat actor could tap the physical fiber connection at the colocation facility. The team must add encryption at the Layer 2 level without replacing the existing Direct Connect connection and without changing the IP addressing scheme or BGP routing configuration. Which solution satisfies all requirements?
tags: Encryption at rest and in transit

answers.A: Deploy an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the existing Direct Connect connection using IKEv2 and AES-256-GCM to add IPsec encryption while keeping existing routing unchanged.
answers.B: Enable MACsec on the Direct Connect dedicated connection by associating a Connection Key Name (CKN) and Connectivity Association Key (CAK), and verify MACsec eligibility for the connection speed and colocation provider.
answers.C: Create a new virtual private gateway, attach a Transit Gateway, and configure an accelerated VPN tunnel using AWS Global Accelerator to achieve hardware-level link encryption.
answers.D: Deploy a pair of third-party virtual firewall appliances in a transit VPC and route all Direct Connect traffic through them to apply AES-256 application-layer encryption.

explanation: B is correct because MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE) provides Layer 2 encryption on Direct Connect dedicated connections. Configuring a CKN/CAK pair on the connection activates MACsec without changing IP addressing or BGP routing, directly addressing the Layer 2 physical-tap threat. A is wrong because IPsec over Direct Connect adds Layer 3 encryption but does not protect against Layer 2 frame-level interception at the physical fiber; it also changes tunnel endpoints. C is wrong because AWS Global Accelerator does not provide hardware-level Layer 2 encryption; this conflates unrelated services. D is wrong because application-layer encryption through virtual firewalls does not provide Layer 2 encryption and requires routing changes that violate the requirements.

stem: A large enterprise wants to federate its 50,000-user Active Directory to AWS using AWS IAM Identity Center. The identity provider is Microsoft AD FS. The company requires that all access to AWS accounts be governed through IAM Identity Center permission sets, that users can only log in using their corporate credentials, and that access logs of all SSO events are available in a central S3 bucket. Which combination of actions satisfies all requirements? (Choose TWO)

answers.A: Configure IAM Identity Center with an external identity provider by uploading the AD FS SAML 2.0 metadata document, set the provisioning method to SCIM or manual sync, and disable IAM Identity Center local users to enforce corporate credential use exclusively.
answers.B: Create IAM SAML identity providers in each member account, configure individual role trust policies referencing AD FS, and use STS AssumeRoleWithSAML directly to bypass IAM Identity Center for federation.
answers.C: Enable AWS CloudTrail in IAM Identity Center and configure a trail that delivers SSO authentication events to an S3 bucket in each individual account where access occurred.
answers.D: Enable AWS CloudTrail at the AWS Organizations management account level with a multi-region organization trail, and configure S3 log delivery to a central logging account. IAM Identity Center management events are captured by CloudTrail automatically.
answers.E: Configure Amazon Cognito as an intermediary identity broker between AD FS and IAM Identity Center to handle SAML-to-OIDC conversion before granting AWS console access.

explanation: A is correct because connecting IAM Identity Center to AD FS via SAML 2.0 metadata and disabling local users ensures all logins use corporate credentials routed through the enterprise IdP. D is correct because IAM Identity Center management events including authentication are captured by CloudTrail automatically. An organization-level multi-region trail with central S3 delivery in a dedicated logging account is the recommended architecture for centralizing SSO audit logs. B is wrong because configuring per-account SAML providers bypasses IAM Identity Center entirely, which is required by the question, and creates unmanageable sprawl. C is wrong because a per-account trail is not necessary; organization trails already capture events from all accounts centrally. E is wrong because Amazon Cognito is not needed as a broker; IAM Identity Center natively supports SAML 2.0 external identity providers.

stem: A SaaS company builds a mobile application that allows users to sign in with Google and Facebook (social identity providers). After authentication, users must call an Amazon API Gateway REST API protected by AWS IAM authorization. The company wants to avoid managing a custom user directory. Which AWS-native approach correctly implements this authentication flow with the least operational overhead?

answers.A: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool and configure Google and Facebook as social identity providers. Create a Cognito identity pool that maps authenticated users to an IAM role. The mobile app exchanges the Cognito token for temporary AWS credentials via the identity pool, then signs API Gateway requests with SigV4 using those credentials.
answers.B: Create IAM OIDC identity providers for Google and Facebook in the AWS account. Configure a Lambda authorizer on API Gateway to validate Google and Facebook tokens directly and return an IAM policy allowing API access.
answers.C: Configure API Gateway to use a Cognito user pool authorizer. The mobile app authenticates with Google or Facebook and retrieves a Cognito user pool JWT, which it includes in the Authorization header without using an identity pool or temporary AWS credentials.
answers.D: Deploy an on-premises LDAP directory, federate it to AWS using AWS Directory Service AD Connector, and configure API Gateway with a custom Lambda authorizer that validates LDAP credentials before allowing access.

explanation: A is correct because Amazon Cognito user pools support Google and Facebook as social identity providers natively. The Cognito identity pool exchanges the user pool token for temporary IAM credentials via the web identity federation flow. The mobile app then calls the IAM-protected API Gateway endpoint using SigV4 signature with those credentials. B is wrong because Lambda authorizers that call external social IdP token introspection endpoints add latency and custom code; this approach also does not produce IAM credentials for SigV4 signing. C is wrong because API Gateway IAM authorization requires SigV4 signing with AWS credentials, not a Cognito JWT; a user pool authorizer (JWT validation) would work only if IAM authorization is not the requirement. D is wrong because LDAP and AD Connector are inappropriate for mobile social logins and introduce unnecessary infrastructure complexity.

stem: A company requires that encryption keys used for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB data never leave a hardware security module. Compliance auditors require that key material be generated inside FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware and that the company retains full control of the key lifecycle, including the ability to immediately revoke all decryption access. The company currently uses SSE-KMS with AWS managed keys. Which change satisfies all compliance requirements?
tags: Encryption at rest and in transit

answers.A: Switch from AWS managed keys to customer managed KMS keys with automatic annual key rotation enabled. Import the key material from an on-premises HSM into the KMS key to maintain control over key material.
answers.B: Use SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys) so that key material is managed entirely outside AWS. The application provides the encryption key with each S3 API request.
answers.C: Use SSE-S3 with KMS envelope encryption and enable S3 Object Lock on the bucket to prevent key deletion and object modification. Rotate the S3-managed key automatically through bucket settings to ensure access revocation.
answers.D: Provision an AWS CloudHSM cluster, create a KMS custom key store backed by the CloudHSM cluster, create a customer managed KMS key in that key store, and configure S3 default bucket encryption and DynamoDB to use this key. Key material is generated and stored exclusively in the CloudHSM hardware.

explanation: D is correct because a KMS custom key store backed by AWS CloudHSM ensures that key material is generated and stored inside the CloudHSM cluster, which is FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated. The company retains full control of the CloudHSM cluster, and deleting the key from the custom key store or destroying the cluster immediately prevents decryption. A is wrong because importing key material into a KMS key copies it into KMS infrastructure; KMS can then use it without the source HSM being involved, so keys do not exclusively reside in hardware. B is wrong because SSE-C means the application holds the key in memory per request, which is operationally burdensome and does not meet hardware-backed storage requirements. C is wrong because SSE-S3 with S3 Object Lock does not address key material hardware residency requirements or FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance.

stem: A company uses a customer managed AWS KMS key to encrypt data in Amazon S3 and DynamoDB. A security review finds that the Lambda execution role for a data processing function has kms:Decrypt permissions with a wildcard resource, allowing decryption with any KMS key in the account. The security team must restrict the Lambda role to only the specific intended CMK while allowing other Lambda functions to continue using their own keys without disruption. Which approach enforces least privilege most directly?

answers.A: Attach a permission boundary to the Lambda execution role that allows kms:Decrypt only on the specific CMK ARN. Leave the wildcard resource in the role inline policy unchanged.
answers.B: Update the Lambda execution role IAM policy to replace the wildcard resource with the specific CMK ARN, granting kms:Decrypt only on that key. Verify that the KMS key policy also grants the Lambda role kms:Decrypt access.
answers.C: Add a Deny condition to the KMS key policy on the specific CMK that blocks all principals except the Lambda execution role ARN. Leave the Lambda role policy unchanged with the wildcard resource.
answers.D: Create a KMS grant on the specific CMK granting kms:Decrypt to the Lambda execution role and remove all kms:Decrypt permissions from the Lambda role IAM policy, relying solely on the grant for access.

explanation: B is correct because IAM access to KMS keys requires both a permissive IAM policy and a KMS key policy. Updating the Lambda role IAM policy to specify the exact CMK ARN instead of a wildcard implements least privilege at the IAM layer. Verifying the KMS key policy grants the role access ensures the full authorization chain works correctly. A is wrong because permission boundaries define the maximum permissions a role can have but do not replace the actual role policy; the wildcard policy is still in effect up to the boundary limit, meaning the role can still decrypt using other keys unless the boundary prevents it, but the question asks to restrict permissions properly. C is wrong because adding a Deny to the KMS key policy for that specific CMK would actually prevent the Lambda from using that key, which is the opposite of the intent. D is wrong because KMS grants without any IAM kms:Decrypt permission can work only if the key policy grants access to the account (not just the role), which is an architectural change that may create unintended access.

stem: A startup stores database passwords for three Amazon RDS instances directly in Lambda environment variables. The security team wants to migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. During rotation, the Lambda functions must never experience authentication failures, even when multiple invocations occur simultaneously while a rotation Lambda is mid-cycle. Which rotation strategy eliminates the authentication failure window?
tags: AWS Secrets Manager secret lifecycle management

answers.A: Use single-user rotation. Secrets Manager rotates the password and updates the secret atomically, so all Lambda invocations immediately retrieve the new password with no downtime.
answers.B: Use single-user rotation with a rotation window scheduled during off-peak hours. Lambda invocations during the rotation window are automatically queued by Amazon SQS until rotation completes.
answers.C: Use multi-user rotation. Secrets Manager alternates between two database users (for example, appuser1 and appuser2). The active secret always points to the user whose password was set in a previous rotation cycle, so the current secret is always valid throughout the rotation of the alternate user.
answers.D: Configure Secrets Manager to rotate the secret and trigger an EventBridge rule that updates the Lambda environment variable automatically after each rotation event completes.

explanation: C is correct because multi-user rotation is the Secrets Manager pattern designed to eliminate authentication failures during rotation. It maintains two database users; while one user password is being rotated, the active secret always points to the other user whose credentials are known-good from a prior rotation. Lambda invocations always receive valid credentials. A is wrong because single-user rotation has a brief window between when the database password is changed and when the Secrets Manager secret value is updated; concurrent Lambda invocations that have cached the old password may fail during this window. B is wrong because Lambda invocations are not automatically queued by Amazon SQS during Secrets Manager rotation; this behavior is fabricated. D is wrong because updating Lambda environment variables causes a function configuration update, which may cause invocations to restart, and environment variable propagation is not instantaneous.

stem: A DevOps team runs a CI/CD pipeline using AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to deploy infrastructure via CloudFormation. A recent audit found that developers can merge code to the main branch without any security scanning, and CloudFormation templates containing overly permissive IAM policies have reached production. The security team must enforce automated security checks that block deployments with critical findings before CloudFormation changes reach production, with minimal disruption to the existing pipeline. Which solution achieves this?

answers.A: Add a CodeBuild stage in CodePipeline before the CloudFormation deploy stage. Configure the CodeBuild project to run a static analysis tool (such as cfn-nag or Checkov) against the CloudFormation templates and return a non-zero exit code on critical findings, causing the pipeline stage to fail and block deployment.
answers.B: Enable the AWS Config managed rule cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check to evaluate CloudFormation stacks after deployment and trigger an SNS notification if policy violations are detected, then manually review and roll back if needed.
answers.C: Configure a CloudFormation stack policy on the production stack to deny changes to IAM resources. Developers must submit a separate change request for IAM updates, which is reviewed out of band.
answers.D: Use AWS CloudFormation Guard rules evaluated as a pre-commit hook on each developer workstation, providing immediate feedback during development. Developers are instructed to resolve all Guard rule failures before pushing code to the main branch.

explanation: A is correct because adding a CodeBuild security scanning stage before the CloudFormation deploy action is the standard CI/CD preventive security gate pattern. Static analysis tools like cfn-nag or Checkov analyze templates for IAM misconfigurations and fail the build on critical findings, blocking the pipeline without disrupting its overall structure. B is wrong because AWS Config evaluates resources post-deployment; the overly permissive policy is already in production by the time a violation is detected. Post-deployment detection is reactive, not preventive. C is wrong because a CloudFormation stack policy restricts updates to specific resource types uniformly but does not perform intelligent security scanning; it blocks all IAM changes rather than scanning for violations. D is wrong because pre-commit hooks on developer workstations are easily bypassed and are not enforced server-side at the pipeline level.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy a standardized security baseline across 200 AWS member accounts in an Organization. A new requirement mandates that all EC2 instances launched in any account must use only pre-approved AMIs. The security team must enforce this requirement without modifying existing CloudFormation templates and with the least ongoing maintenance overhead. Which approach enforces the AMI restriction organization-wide?

answers.A: Add a new StackSet that deploys an AWS Config custom rule to each account. The rule checks that running EC2 instances use approved AMIs and sends SNS notifications for violations requiring manual remediation.
answers.B: Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that includes a Deny statement for ec2:RunInstances with a condition that the ec2:ImageId is not in the approved AMI list. Attach the SCP to the root OU or the applicable OU containing the 200 accounts.
answers.C: Deploy an Amazon EventBridge rule in each account that triggers a Lambda function to terminate EC2 instances not launched from approved AMIs within 60 seconds of the launch event.
answers.D: Update all existing CloudFormation templates to add an AMI parameter with an AllowedValues constraint restricted to approved AMIs, and redeploy the updated templates via StackSets to all accounts.

explanation: B is correct because SCPs applied at the root or OU level are enforced as organizational guardrails that no account can override. Using the ec2:ImageId condition key in an SCP Deny statement prevents RunInstances calls with unapproved AMIs, regardless of which template or user initiates the launch. This requires no changes to existing templates, and maintenance is limited to updating the AMI list in the SCP when new AMIs are approved. A is wrong because AWS Config rules are detective controls that identify violations after the fact; the EC2 instance is already running and requires manual remediation. C is wrong because the EventBridge-plus-Lambda approach is reactive and causes disruption because instances launch first before being terminated. D is wrong because updating 200 accounts CloudFormation templates is high-maintenance and does not prevent resources launched outside of CloudFormation.

stem: A healthcare company must demonstrate continuous HIPAA compliance across 50 AWS accounts to external compliance officers. The compliance team needs: a dashboard of Config rule violations related to encryption and access controls, automatically collected evidence for auditors, and audit reports that map AWS controls to HIPAA requirements. Which combination of AWS services most directly satisfies all three needs?
tags: Compliance frameworks (CIS, NIST, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR)

answers.A: Enable AWS Security Hub with the FSBP standard in all accounts, use Security Hub finding aggregation to centralize findings, and export the findings to Amazon S3. The compliance team manually maps FSBP controls to HIPAA requirements.
answers.B: Deploy AWS Config aggregators at the management account to collect compliance data from all accounts, create custom Config rules for HIPAA-specific controls, and use Amazon QuickSight to build dashboards from Config data in S3.
answers.C: Use AWS Trusted Advisor security checks across all accounts, export findings via the AWS Support API, and manually compile a HIPAA compliance report from the data.
answers.D: Enable AWS Config with a delegated aggregator account to collect compliance data. Use AWS Audit Manager with a prebuilt HIPAA framework to automatically collect evidence from Config, CloudTrail, and Security Hub, and generate assessment reports with control-to-HIPAA mappings.

explanation: D is correct because AWS Audit Manager is purpose-built for compliance assessment. It has a prebuilt HIPAA framework that maps AWS controls to HIPAA requirements. Audit Manager automatically collects evidence from AWS Config, CloudTrail, Security Hub, and other sources across multiple accounts and generates audit-ready assessment reports, satisfying all three requirements. A is wrong because Security Hub does not provide automated HIPAA control mapping or generate audit-ready evidence reports; it requires manual mapping. B is wrong because custom Config rules and QuickSight dashboards cover only the dashboard requirement; the approach lacks HIPAA control mapping and automatic audit evidence collection. C is wrong because Trusted Advisor does not provide HIPAA framework mapping, does not aggregate across 50 accounts natively, and its findings are not structured as audit evidence.

stem: An organization must provide external auditors with proof that its AWS CloudTrail logs have not been modified since collection, and also provide the auditors with official compliance documents (SOC 2 Type II report, PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance) applicable to the AWS services it uses. Which combination of AWS capabilities provides both with the least effort?
tags: Compliance frameworks (CIS, NIST, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR)

answers.A: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation. Download compliance reports from the AWS Compliance Programs website and provide the URLs to auditors as evidence.
answers.B: Use Amazon Macie to scan the CloudTrail log S3 bucket for modifications and send alerts via SNS. Subscribe to AWS compliance notification emails for report updates.
answers.C: Enable AWS CloudTrail log file integrity validation using SHA-256 hash chaining. Provide auditors with the digest files stored in S3 as tamper evidence. Access and download the applicable compliance reports (SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS AOC) directly from AWS Artifact and provide them to auditors.
answers.D: Store CloudTrail logs in an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled in compliance mode to prevent tampering. Generate compliance certificates by submitting a formal request to AWS Support.

explanation: C is correct because CloudTrail log file integrity validation creates SHA-256 digest files that chain together, allowing auditors to mathematically verify that no log files were modified or deleted since delivery. AWS Artifact is the official AWS service for accessing and downloading compliance reports including SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS attestations, which can be shared directly with auditors. A is wrong because providing URLs to a webpage does not constitute downloadable audit evidence that auditors can independently verify. B is wrong because Amazon Macie is a data classification service, not a log integrity tool; it cannot generate hash-chain evidence of log integrity. D is wrong because S3 Object Lock prevents deletion but does not provide a mathematical proof-of-integrity chain; compliance reports are obtained from AWS Artifact, not AWS Support requests.

stem: A gaming company platform experiences DDoS attacks during peak tournament events with volumetric attack traffic exceeding 400 Gbps. The company uses Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and an Application Load Balancer. Despite having AWS Shield Standard, the attacks cause availability degradation. The security team must ensure the infrastructure can withstand large volumetric attacks and have 24/7 access to AWS DDoS mitigation experts during attacks. Which set of actions achieves these goals?
tags: AWS Shield (Standard and Advanced) DDoS protection

answers.A: Upgrade to AWS Shield Advanced, enroll the CloudFront distribution and ALB as protected resources, enable automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation with AWS WAF, and grant the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT) IAM permissions to assist during active attacks.
answers.B: Add more CloudFront edge locations using geographic restrictions, increase the WAF rate-based rule threshold to 10,000 requests per 5 minutes, and enable CloudFront compression to reduce bandwidth during attacks.
answers.C: Configure AWS Global Accelerator as the entry point for all traffic, enable flow logs for real-time attack pattern detection, and use Route 53 health checks to fail over to a secondary region during an attack.
answers.D: Deploy a fleet of EC2 instances running open-source DDoS mitigation software behind the ALB, scale the fleet using Auto Scaling, and use Route 53 latency-based routing to distribute attack traffic.

explanation: A is correct because AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced volumetric DDoS protection beyond Shield Standard, cost protection for scaling during DDoS events, and 24/7 access to the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT). Enrolling the CloudFront distribution and ALB as protected resources and enabling automatic application-layer mitigation through WAF integration addresses both volumetric and application-layer attacks. B is wrong because increasing WAF rate thresholds and adding CloudFront edge locations does not protect against 400 Gbps volumetric attacks that exhaust network capacity; SRT access is also not provided. C is wrong because Global Accelerator improves routing but does not provide volumetric DDoS protection or SRT access at the required scale. D is wrong because self-managed DDoS software on EC2 cannot absorb 400 Gbps before reaching instances, and this approach provides no SRT access.

stem: A company exposes a public REST API through Amazon API Gateway. The API has been receiving HTTP floods from rotating IP addresses that bypass existing WAF IP block rules. The security team wants to automatically block IP addresses that exceed 1,000 requests per 5 minutes and ensure that only known partner IP ranges can call specific premium endpoints regardless of the rate. Which combination of AWS WAF features achieves both goals with the least custom code?

answers.A: Create a Lambda authorizer on API Gateway that counts requests per source IP using an ElastiCache Redis counter. If the count exceeds 1,000 in 5 minutes, the authorizer returns a Deny policy. Require a custom HTTP header for premium endpoints.
answers.B: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the API Gateway stage and configure DDoS response team access. Use API Gateway usage plans with API keys for partner integrations to restrict premium endpoint access.
answers.C: Create a rate-based rule in AWS WAF with a 1,000-request threshold per 5-minute aggregation window and set the action to Block. Create a WAF IP set containing partner IP ranges with an Allow action at a higher priority than the rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the API Gateway stage.
answers.D: Configure API Gateway throttling with a burst limit of 1,000 and a steady-state rate of 200 requests per second at the stage level. Issue API keys to partners and associate them with a usage plan that has elevated rate limits.

explanation: C is correct because AWS WAF rate-based rules natively count requests by IP address and automatically block IPs that exceed the configured threshold with no custom code. An IP set Allow rule at higher priority ensures partner IP addresses bypass the rate-based block, allowing unrestricted premium endpoint access without custom logic. A is wrong because a Lambda authorizer with ElastiCache for IP rate counting requires significant custom code and operational overhead for functionality that WAF provides natively. B is wrong because Shield Advanced protects against volumetric DDoS but does not provide per-IP request counting and automatic blocking; API keys restrict access but do not block flooding IPs. D is wrong because API Gateway throttling applies per stage or per usage plan, not per source IP, and does not automatically block offending IP addresses.

stem: A company is expanding from a single AWS account to a multi-account structure using AWS Organizations. The security team must ensure that: (1) member accounts cannot disable AWS CloudTrail or delete GuardDuty findings, (2) all new accounts automatically receive a security baseline with GuardDuty and Config enabled, and (3) security engineers can investigate incidents in member accounts without maintaining separate IAM users in each account. Which architecture satisfies all three requirements?

answers.A: Create SCPs that deny cloudtrail:StopLogging and guardduty:DeleteFindings at the root OU. Manually deploy a CloudFormation template with the security baseline to each new account. Create cross-account IAM roles in each member account for security engineers.
answers.B: Use AWS Config aggregators to detect when CloudTrail is disabled and trigger a Lambda function to re-enable it. Configure GuardDuty with a delegated administrator and invite all member accounts. Create IAM users with cross-account permissions for security engineers.
answers.C: Deploy SCPs to block disabling CloudTrail and deleting GuardDuty findings. Use a manual account provisioning checklist. Configure IAM Identity Center with permission sets for security engineers.
answers.D: Deploy AWS Control Tower with preventive SCP guardrails that block disabling CloudTrail and deleting GuardDuty findings. Use Account Factory to automatically apply the security baseline to new accounts. Configure IAM Identity Center with a Security Engineer permission set for centralized cross-account federated access.

explanation: D is correct because AWS Control Tower provides all three capabilities integrated: (1) built-in preventive SCP guardrails prevent disabling CloudTrail and protect GuardDuty findings organization-wide, (2) Account Factory automates new account provisioning with a pre-configured security baseline, and (3) IAM Identity Center with permission sets enables centralized, federated cross-account access for security engineers without per-account IAM users. A is wrong because it manually deploys baselines and uses per-account IAM roles requiring ongoing maintenance for each new account and no automated provisioning. B is wrong because Config-plus-Lambda is a reactive detective control, not preventive; IAM users across accounts are operationally expensive. C is wrong because it lacks automated new account provisioning.

stem: A legal services firm stores client case documents in Amazon S3 for 7 years per regulatory requirements. Documents must be immutable once uploaded, and no user including the AWS account root user must be able to delete or overwrite them during the retention period.
